details.body: Label, s. patraM, aMkapatraM, bIjakaM, lepapatraM. v. t. lepapatraM AsaMj c. or anubaMD 3 P.
LABEL (subs.): *lepapatram; bIjakam, Monier Williams.
LABEL (v.): *lepapatraM sajjayati (c. of sajj).
LABEL , s. patraM, sUcakapatraM, aNkapatraM, aNkapawaH, vIjakaM.
To LABEL , v. a. sUcakapatram Aruh (c. 10. -ropayati -yituM) or anubanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM) or banD.
Labial, a. ozWya.
LABIAL: I Adj.: OzWya (f. zWyA).II Subs.: ozWyavarRaH; OzWyam.
LABIAL , a. ozWyaH -zWyA -zWyaM, ozWasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n); ‘a labial letter,’ ozWyaM.
Labio-dental, a. daMto(tO)zWya.
LABIODENTAL , a. dantozWyaH -zWyA -zWyaM, dantOzWyaH &c., dantyozWyaH &c.

Labor (Labour), s. SramaH, pariSramaH, pra-A-yAsaH, kleSaH, kazwaM, duHKaM. 2 udyamaH, u-dyogaH, vyApAraH, vyavasAyaH, cezwA, pra-, yatnaH, utsAhaH. 3 prasUtikAlaH-samayaH, prasavakAlaH, prasavAvasTA; ‘pain of l(abor)’ prasUti-prasava-ve-danA-yAtanA-vyaTA; ‘bodily l(abor)’ vrAtaM, deha-kAya-kleSa-AyAsaH-SramaH; ‘unpaid l(abor)’ vizwi f., AjUH; ‘got by oneʼs l(abor)’ svakazwArjita. v. i. pariSramaM-AyAsaM-kf 8 U, Sram 4 P, pra-, yat 1 A, Dyava-so 4 U, cezw 1 A, udyam 1 P, pravft 1 A, Ayas 1, 4 P, vrAtaM kf, SarIrAyAsaM kf. 2 Kid-kliS-pIq pass., vyaT 1 A. 3 prasavAvasTAyAM vft, (Asanna-prasavA or prAptaprasavavedanA sA strI); ‘l(abor) under’ bAD-aBiBU-Akram-pIq-upahan- pass., ‘l(abor)ing under hundreds of anxieties’ ciMtASatErbADyamAna-aBiBUta; atiBArAkrAMta &c.; ‘l(abor)ing under a disease’ roga-pIqita, rujArta. v. t. mahASrameRa-prayatnena-sAD 5 P or saM-pad c. or kxp c. or vi-DA 3 U or kf or anu-zWA 1 P. 2 kfz 6 U. [Labor]ed, a. Srama-yatna-kazwa-sidDa, yatna-Srama-pUrva, prayatna-kfta. [Labor]er, s. kftaSramaH, karmin m., vyavasA-yin m., kArmaH. 2 karmakaraH, karmakAraH, BftakaH, vEtanikaH, Bfti-BaraRya-Buj m. 3 kfzakaH, kfzIvalaH; See Farmer. Laborious, a. Srama-AyAsa-kazwa-sADya, kazwa-AyAsa-prad, pIqAkara (rI f.), duHKasADya, kazwa. 2 A-yAsin, kftaSrama, Srama-udyoga-karma-SIla, udya-min, udyogin, sodyama, sodyoga, sotsAha; See Industrious. [Laborious]ly, adv. SrameRa, Srama-AyAsa-pUrvaM, A-pra-yAsena, sayatnaM, sodyogaM, sodyamaM, sotsAhaM, kazwena, kfcCreRa. [Laborious]ness, s. SramasADyatA. 2 udyogaH, udyamaH, vyavasAyaH, udyogaSIlatA. Laboratory, s. rasakriyAsTAnaM, rasasaMskAraSAlA. 2 udyoga-Silpa-SAlA-gfhaM.

LABOR , s. (Exertion) utsAhaH, udyogaH, yatnaH, prayatnaH, vyavasAyaH, aDyavasAyaH, udyamaH, AyAsaH, karmma n. (n), kriyA, pravfttiH f., vyApAraH, cezwA. — (Toil) AyAsaH, prayAsaH, kleSaH, SramaH, pariSramaH, kazwaM, duHKaM, nityaSramaH, nityakleSaH. — (Bodily or manual labor) kAyakleSaH, dehakleSaH, SarIrAyAsaH, SarIrakleSaH, SarIraSramaH, vrAtaM. — (Unpaid labor) vizwiH, AjUH f. — (Travail, childbirth) prasavavedanA, prasUti- vedanA, garBavedanA, prasavayAtanA, prasavakAlaH, prasUtikAlaH; ‘acquired by one's own labor,’ svakazwArjitaH -tA -taM.

To LABOR , v. n. (Exert strength, make effort) yat (c. 1. yatate -tituM), prayat, vyavaso (c. 4. -syati -sAtuM), udyam (c. 1. -yacCati -yantuM) cezw (c. 1. cezwate -zwituM), vicezw, udyogaM kf, utsAhaM kf, yatnaM kf, vyava- sAyaM kf, AyAsaM kf. — (Toil) Ayas (c. 4. -yasyati -yasituM), AyAsaM kf, Sram (c. 4. SrAmyati, SramituM), pariSram, kliS (c. 4. kliSyate, kleSituM), parikliS, SarIrAyAsaM kf, vrAtaM kf, SarIrAyAsena karmma kf, kazwaM kf. — (Be in distress) kliS, vyaT (c. 1. vyaTate -TituM), pIq in pass. (pIqyate), tap in pass. (tapyate), kfcCra (nom. kfcCrAyate), Kid in pass. (Kidyate), pariKid. — (Be in travail) prAptaprasavavedanABU, prAptagarBavedanABU, prAptaprasavakAlA BU. — (Labor under) upahan in pass. (-hanyate), pIq in pass. (pIqyate), upahataH -tA -taM BU, pIqitaH -tA -taM BU; ‘to labor [Page433-a+ 51] under a disease,’ rogapIqitaH -tA -taM BU, rogArttaH -rttA -rttaM BU.

To LABOR , v. a. (Form with labor) mahAyatnena or bahuSrameRa or atyA- yAsena kf or saMskf or parizkf or sAD (c. 10. sADayati -yituM) or sidDIkf or kxp (c. 10. kalpayati -yituM) or viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), yatnena sev (c. 1. sevate -vituM) or upasev or anuzWA (c. 1. -tizWati -zWAtuM) or AsTA. — (Till, cultivate) kfz (c. 6. kfzati, krazwuM).
LABORATORY: Of chemists: *karmakulam and sim. comp.s.
LABORATORY , s. (Work-room) udyogaSAlA, udyogagfhaM, SilpaSAlA. — (House for chemical experiments) rasAyanakarmmagfhaM, rasAyana- karmmaSAlA, rasasaMskAraSAlA.
LABORED , p. p. or a. SramasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, AyAsasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, yatnasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, kazwasidDaH &c., yatnapUrvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM, SramapUrvvaH &c., AyA- sapUrvvaH &c.

LABORER , s. (One engaged in any toilsome work) AyAsI m. (n), kftAyAsaH, SramI m. (n), kftaSramaH, udyogI m. (n), kftodyogaH, vyavasAyI m. (n), karmmI m. (n), kArmmaH. — (A hired or day laborer) vrAtInaH, karmmakaraH, karmmakAraH -rakaH, karmmakArI m. (n), BftakaH, BftaH, BftiBuk m. (j), vEtanikaH, BaraRyaBuk m., vetanArTI m. (n), vetanagrAhI m. (n), vasnikaH. — (Cultivator of soil) kfzakaH, karzakaH, kzetrikaH, kzetrI m. (n), kzetrakarzakaH, kInASaH, kfzIbalaH.

LABORING , part. or a. kftaSramaH -mA -maM, kftAyAsaH -sA -saM, SramakArI -riRI -ri (n); ‘a laboring man.’ See LABORER. (Labor- ing under) upahataH -tA -taM, pIqitaH -tA -taM; ‘laboring under a disease,’ rogapIqitaH -tA -taM.
LABORIOUS: I Requiring labour:(1) Srama- sADya (f. DyA);(2) prayAsakaraH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s.II Industrious: q. v.: pariSramin (f. RI).

LABORIOUS , a. (Using labor, industrious) AyAsI -sinI -si (n), SramI -miRI -mi (n), pariSramI &c., kftaSramaH -mA -maM, SramaSIlaH -lA -laM, bahuSramaH -mA -maM, udyogI -ginI -gi (n), udyogaSIlaH -lA -laM, utsAhI -hinI -hi (n), karmmaSIlaH -lA -laM, karmmI -rmmiRI -rmmi (n), kArmmaH -rmmI -rmmaM, karmmodyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, sayatnaH -tnA -tnaM, yatnaSIlaH -lA -laM, prayatnavAn -vatI -vat (t), vyavasAyI -yinI -yi (n), udyamI &c., sotsAhaH -hA -haM, karmmaparAyaRaH -RA -RaM, SramasahaH -hA -haM, SrAmikaH -kI -kaM, analasaH -sA -saM, nirAlasyaH -syA -syaM, prayAsaBAk m. f. n. (j), sodyogaH -gA -gaM. — (Requiring labor) SramasADyaH -DyA -DyaM, kazwasADyaH -DyA -DyaM, AyAsasADyaH &c., SramasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, duHsADyaH &c., kaWinaH -nA -naM, duHKena or kfcCreRa sADyaH -DyA -DyaM, duHKasADyaH &c., kazwaH -zwA -zwaM.
LABORIOUSLY: (1) pariSrameRa;(2) SramapUrvam;(3) saprayAsam.
LABORIOUSLY , adv. SrameRa, bahuSrameRa, saSramaM, SramapUrvvaM, AyAsena, prayAsena, sAyAsaM, kazwena, kfcCreRa, udyamena, sotsAhaM, sodyogaM, yatnena, yatnatas, sayatnaM.
LABORIOUSNESS: I Toilsomeness: prayAsakaratA; etc.II Industry: q. v.

LABORIOUSNESS , s. (Diligence) AyAsaSIlatA, udyogaSIlatA, karmma- SIlatA, udyogaH, sodyogatvaM, yatnaH, sayatnatA, vyavasAyaH, udyamaH. — (Toilsomeness) SramasADyatA, kazwasADyatA, AyAsasADyatA, duHKasADyatvaM, sakazwatvaM, kazwiH f.

LABOUR (v.): I To toil:(1) pariSramaM karoti; (2) AyAsaM karoti.II To work: karma karoti. III To strive: yatnaM or udyogaM karoti.IV To be in travail: prasavAvasTAyAM vartate.V To 1. under, suffer: bADyate (pass. of bAD) or bADitaH (tA, taM).

LABOUR (subs.): I Toil:(1) SramaH, pari-, languid with l.: pariSramakrAnta (f. ntA), Ki. iv. 17.;(2) AyAsaH or prayAsaH (= exertion), then why vain l.: tat kiM vfTA prayAsena, P.II. Work: q. v.: karman (n.).III Of childbirth: prasavA- vasTA (the state); prasavavedanA (of the pains).
LABOURED (adj.): (1) SramasidDa (f. dDA) (?); (2) AyAsasidDa (f. dDA) (?).
LABOURER: (1) karmakaraH, will do work like l. s: karma karmakaravat karizyati, Si.;(2) karmAjIvaH;(3) karmajIvI, artisans and l. s: SilpinaH karmajIvinaSca, V. s.
LABURNUM: sundaravfkzaviSezaH; lAvaRyaH.
Labyrinth, s. atigahanaH pradeSaH, dustaraM or sugahanaM sTAnaM, aSakyanirgamaH pradeSaH, gahanaM. [Labyrinth]ian, a. gahana, sudustara.
LABYRINTH: durlakzyanirgamA vAwI or vAwikA.

LABYRINTH , s. gahanaM, sugahanasTAnaM, dustarasTAnaM, sudustarasTAnaM, Bramajanako bahuvyatyastamArgaH pradeSaH, BrAntijanako bahuviparItamArgaH pradeSaH or bahuva- kramArgo BUBiBAgaH, aSakyanirgamaH pradeSaH.
LABYRINTHIAN, LABYRINTHINE: atigahanaH (nA, naM) (?).
LABYRINTHIAN , a. gahanaH -nA -naM, sugahanaH -nA -naM, sudustaraH -rA -raM.
Lac, s. lA(rA)kzA, alaktaH-ktakaH, jatu n., yAvaH, drumAmayaH. 2 lakzaM.
LAC: I The substance:(1) lAkzA;(2) alaktaH; (3) jAtu, -kam (n.).II The number: lakzam.

LAC , s. (A resinous substance used as a red dye, produced mainly upon the Banyan-tree by the insect Coccus lacca, analogous to the cochineal insect. The following names apply either to the dye or the insect, lAkzA, rAkzA, alaktaH -ktakaM, laktakaM, jatu n., jatukaM, jaturasaH, yAvaH -vakaH, kArpawaH, mucakaH, garADikA, drumavyADiH m., drumAmayaH, kIwajA, kfmiH m., titiBaH; [Page433-b+ 51] ‘made of lac,’ lAkzikaH -kI -kaM; ‘liquified lac dye,’ alaktarasaH. — (The number). See LACK.
Lace, s. sUtraM, taMtuH, guRaH. 2 sUtrajAlaM, jAlA-BaraRaM, jAlarUpaM, vastrABaraRaM. v. t. sUtreRa baMD 9 P, or saMyuj 7 U, 10 or saMSliz c. 2 jAlABaraREH BUz 10 or alaM-kf 8 U.
LACE (subs.): I A string or cord: sUtram. II A fabric: *sUtrajAlam.
LACE (v.): sUtrajAlena maRqayati (maRq, c. 10.), “l. d with silver” *rajatajAlamaRqitaH (tA, taM): v. Also to fasten.
LACE , s. (Texture of interwoven threads) jAlaM, jAlikA, jAlakaM, jAlABaraRaM, jAlarUpaM sUkzmatantunirmmitaM vastrABaraRaM or vastrAYcalaM. — (String, cord) sUtraM, tantuH m., guRaH.

To LACE , v. a. (Fasten with a string) sUtreRa banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM) or saMyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM) or saMSliz (c. 10. -Slezayati -yituM), sUtrabadDaM -dDAM -dDaM kf. — (Adorn with lace) jAlABaraREr alaNkf or BUz (c. 10. BUzayati -yituM).
LACEMAKER: *jAlakarmakaraH; sUtrajAlakaraH.
LACEMAN , s. jAlABaraRavikrayI m. (n), jAlAlaNkAravikrayI m., jAla- vikretA m. (tf).
LACERABLE , a. vidAraRIyaH -yA -yaM, vidAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, dAraRIyaH -yA -yaM.
Lacerate, v. t. dF 9 P, 10, nirBid 7 P, vyavacCid 7 P, vi-paw 10, kft 6 P; See Tear. [Lacerat]ion, s. vidAraH-raRaM, nirBedaH, vipA-wanaM. 2 BedaH, CidraM, saMDiH.
LACERATE: Binatti (Bid, c. 7.): v. To rend, tear. L. d wound: Binnam, Sr.

To LACERATE , v. a. dF (c. 9. dfRAti, darituM -rItuM, c. 10. dArayati -yituM), vidF, avadF, viBid (c. 7. -Binatti -BettuM), nirBid, vyavaCid (c. 7. -Cinatti -CettuM), nikft (c. 6. -kfntati -karttituM), vinikft, vidal (c. 10. -dalayati -yituM), vidalIkf, vraSc (c. 6. vfScati, vraScituM), pravraSc; ‘to be lacerated,’ vidF in pass. (-dIryyate).

LACERATED , p. p. vidAritaH -tA -taM, vidIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, dAritaH -tA -taM, dIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, pravidAritaH -tA -taM, viBinnaH -nnA -nnaM, BinnaH -nnA -nnaM, vidalitaH -tA -taM, dalitaH -tA -taM, pAwitaH -tA -taM, vipAwitaH -tA -taM, vidalIkftaH -tA -taM.
LACERATION: I The act:(1) Bedanam;(2) viBedaH;(3) vidAraRam;(4) pAwanam, vi-.II The breach made: BedaH, vi-.
LACERATION , s. (The act of tearing) vidAraH -raRaM -RA, vidaraH, dAraRaM, vidalIkaraRaM, pravidAraRaM, viBedaH, vraScanaM, pAwanaM, vipAwanaM. — (The rent made) CidraM, BedaH, vidalaM.
Laches, s. kAlAtipAtaH, kAlavyayaH; upekzA.
Lachrymal, a. aSrupravAhin, aSrUtpAdin. 2 aSrusaMbaMDin. Lachrymatory, s. aSrupAtraM BAjanaM. Lachrymose, a. sAsra, bAzpAkula.
LACHRYMAL , a. (Secreting tears) aSrujanakaH -kA -kaM, aSrUtpAdakaH -kA -kaM, aSruvAhakaH -kA -kaM. — (Pertaining to tears) aSrusambanDI nDinI -nDi (n).

sanskrit.word: मृतजनमित्रैः पातितानाम् अश्रूणां काचादिनिर्म्मितपात्रं तच्च पूर्व्वकाले
sanskrit.iast: mṛtajanamitraiḥ pātitānām aśrūṇāṃ kācādinirmmitapātraṃ tacca pūrvvakāle

details.body: LACHRYMATORY , s. aSrupAtraM, aSruBAjanaM, nayanavAzpADAraH, maraRakAle mftajanamitrEH pAtitAnAm aSrURAM kAcAdinirmmitapAtraM tacca pUrvvakAle mftaSarIreRa saha BUmO nyaKanyata.
LACHRYMOSE , a. aSrumayaH -yI -yaM, sASraH -SrA -SraM, vAzpAkulaH -lA -laM.

Lack, v. na DA 3 U or Df 1 P or Bf 3 U; gen. ex. by hIna, vahita, varjita, SUnya in comp., or a or nir pr.; ‘l(ack)s wisdom’ nirbudDiH, ajYAnaH, budDihInaH, &c. s. aBAvaH, hInatA, nyUnatA, virahaH, SUnyatA. 2 prayojanaM; ‘l(ack)-lustre’ nizpraBa, atejas, maMdacCAya, malinakAMti; ‘l(ack)-brain’ nirbudDiH, matihInaH, mUQaH, mUrKaH.
LACK (subs.): aBAvaH: v. Want, deficiency.

To LACK , v. a. or n. (Be destitute of) hInaH -nA -naM or vihInaH -nA -naM or parihIRaH -RA -RaM or rahitaH -tA -taM or virahitaH -tA -taM or varjitaH -tA -taM or vivarjitaH -tA -taM or SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM or apetaH -tA -taM BU or as, hA in pass. (hIyate) or vihA with abl. or instr. c., viyuj in pass. (-yujyate) with instr. c., or expressed by a or nir prefixed; as, ‘he lacks wisdom,’ budDihInaH or budDirahitaH or nirbudDir asti; ‘he lacks means,’ asADano'sti. — (Not to have) na DA (c. 3. daDAti, Datte, DAtuM), na Df (c. 10. DArayati -yituM), na viDA. — (Be wanting) nyUnIBU, nyUnaH -nA -naM BU or as, nyUnatA BU or as, prayojanam as; ‘what lack I yet?’ mama kiM nyUnaM or mama kena prayojanaM.
LACK , s. (Want, destitution) hInatA, rahitatvaM, SUnyatA, aBAvaH, asamBavaH, virahaH, avizayaH, nyUnatA. — (Need) prayojanaM. — (One hundred thousand) lakzaM -kzA, lakzyaM.
LACK-A-DAISICAL , a. DyAnaparaH -rA -raM, udvignamanAH -nAH -naH (s), unmanAH &c., cintAkulaH -lA -laM, vizAdI -dinI -di (n), utkaRWitaH -tA -taM.
LACK-A-DAY: aho durdinam: v. Alas.
LACK-A-DAY , exclam. aho, ahovat, ahaha, hanta, A, hA, kazwaM.
LACK-BRAIN: nirbudDi (mfn.): v. Fool.
LACK-LUSTRE , a. nistejAH -jAH -jaH (s), tejohInaH -nA -naM, nizpraBaH -BA -BaM, apraBaH -BA -BaM, mandacCAyaH -yA -yaM, mandakAntaH -ntA -ntaM, mali- napraBaH -BA -BaM.
Lack-a-daisical, a. DyAnapara-magna, ciMtA-kula, utkaMWita, vizaRRa.
Lack-a-day, interj. aho, haMta, hA, ahaha, bata.
LACKBRAIN , s. nirbudDiH m., abudDiH m., jYAnahInaH, mUrKaH, mUQaH.
Lacker, Lacquer, v. t. lAkzArasena Cad 10. kukkuBena lip 6 P.
LACKER , s. (Kind of varnish) lAkzAdinirmmitaH kukkuBakaviSezaH, lAkzA.
To LACKER , v. a. pUrvvoktakukkuBakena lip (c. 6. limpati, leptuM).
Lackey, s. cewaH, dAsaH, BftyaH, pArzRigrAhaH, pArSvAnucaraH.
LACKEY: cewaH (= servant.).
LACKEY , s. pArSvAnucaraH, paricaraH, kiNkaraH, prezyaH, BftyaH, dAsaH.
To LACKEY , v. a. or n. upacar (c. 1. -carati -rituM), pArSve paricar, pArSvAnucaro BU.

Laconic, [Laconic]al, a. saMkzipta, laGu, alpa-mita-Sabdaka, avistIrRa, sAMkzepika (kI f.); ‘l(aconic) message’ laGusaMdeSapadA sarasvatI. 2 alpa-mita-BAzin. [Laconic]ally, adv. saMkzepeRa, saMkzepataH, avistareRa, mitoktyA. [Laconic]ism, Laconism, s. lAGavaM; laGUkti f., saMkzepoktiH; mitavAkyaM-BAzaRaM.
LACONIC: (1) laGu (mfn.);(2) saMkzipta (f. ptA) (= concise).

LACONIC , LACONICAL, a. (Concise, expressed in few words) saMkziptaH -ptA -ptaM, sAMkzepikaH -kI -kaM, avistIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, alpaSabdakaH -kA -kaM, parimitaSabdaH -bdA -bdaM, parimitavAkyaH -kyA -kyaM, parimitoktiH -ktiH -kti, saMkziptoktiH -ktiH -kti, mitaSabdakaH -kA -kaM, abahuSabdaH -bdA -bdaM. — (Laconic speaker) parimitaBAzI -ziRI -zi (n), mitaBAzI &c., saMkziptaBAzI &c., saMkziptavaktA -ktrI -ktf (ktf), avistIrRavaktA &c., alpaBAzI &c.
LACONICALLY: (1) lAGavena;(2) salAGavam;(3) saMkzepeRa (= concisely).
LACONICALLY , adv. saMkzepatas, saMkzepeRa, avistareRa, avistaraSas, parimi- toktyA, mitoktyA, samAsatas.
LACONISM: I The style: lAGavam, Ki.II A saying: laGUktiH, etc.
LACONISM , LACONICISM, s. saMkziptoktiH f., saMkziptavAkyaM, alpaSabdakavAkyaM, mitaSabdakavAkyaM, parimitavAkyaM, avistIrRavAkyaM, saMkzepavAkyaM.
LACQUER (LACKER) (subs.): *lAkzakaRa (lAkzA = lac).
LACQUER (LACKER) (v.): *lAkzakeRa limpati (lip, c. 6.).
Lactary, s. kzIrasTAnaM, godugDasTAnaM.
LACTARY , a. kzIrI -riRI -ri (n), kzIraviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.

LAKSHMĪ , s. (The goddess of fortune or prosperity, wife of the god Viṣṇu. She is said also to preside over beauty; and in this respect, as well as in the story of her birth, agrees in character with Venus. She was born, according to the usual account, from the ocean, when churned by [Page435-a+ 51] the gods and Asuras; and emerged from the foam of the sea, seated on a full-blown lotus, and holding a lotus in her hand. Her countenance is represented as in- comparably beautiful. As presiding over abundance she resembles Ceres. She is by some considered to be the daughter of Daksha, and by others of Bhrigu. Some- times she is regarded as the wife of Dharma. As god- dess of prosperity she is called) lakzmIH f., SrIH f. — (As wife of Viṣṇu) vizRuvallaBA, haripriyA, vEzRavI. — (The ocean-born) jalaDijA, kzIrAbDijA, kzIrAbDitanayA. — (As seated on and holding the lotus, or as identified with this flower, which is the symbol of prosperity) padmA, kamalA, padmAlayA, padmavAsA, padmasnuzA. — (As wife of Viṣṇu in the avatār of Krishna) rukmiRI. — (As mother of Kāmadeva) mAyA. — (As wife of Nārāyana) nArAyaRI. — (As wife of Viṣṇu in the avatār of Rāmachandra) sItA. — (As mother of the world) lokamAtA f. (tf), mAtA. — (As wife of Viṣṇu in the Varāha avatār) vArAhI. — (The fickle one, a name applied to Lakṣmī as goddess of fortune) capalA, caYcalA, calA, lolA. — (As identified with a celebrated Apsaras) ramBA. Other names of this goddess are, ramA, indirA, mA, netrI, hIrA, laYjA.

LASH , s. (Thong) kazA, kaSA, pratizkazaH -SaH, balisaNgaH, carmmabanDaH, carmmarajjuH m. f., varatrA, nadDrI, vaDrI, badDrI, vArdDaM -rdDI. — (Stroke with a whip) kazAGAtaH, kazAprahAraH, kazAtAqanaM. — (Stroke of satire) vAgasiH f.

To LASH , v. a. (Strike with a lash) kazayA or carmmarajvA taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM) or Ahan (c. 2. -hanti -ntuM) or prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), kaSa (nom. kaSayati -yituM), kazAGAtaM kf. — (Beat, shake about) viDU (c. 5. -DUnoti -DavituM), DU, vical (c. 10. -cAlayati -yituM); ‘he [Page438-b+ 51] lashes his tail,’ pucCaM DUnoti. — (Tie or bind with a rope) rajjunA or rajvA banD (c. 9. banDAti, bandDuM), rajjubadDaM -dDAM -dDaM kf. — (Censure with severity) aruntudavAcA or tIkzRavAkyEH or tigma- vAcA nind (c. 1. nindati -ndituM).
To LASH , v. n. kazAGAtaM kf, kazAtAqanaM kf. — (Lash out, run into excess) maryyAdAm atikram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM), utkram, vyutkram, avaDim aticar (c. 1. -carati -rituM).
LASHED , p. p. kazAhataH -tA -taM, kazAtAqitaH -tA -taM; ‘worthy of being lashed,’ kaSyaH -SyA -SyaM, kaSArhaH -rhA -rhaM. — (Made fast) rajjubadDaH -dDA -dDaM.
Lass, s. taruRI, kanyA, bAlA, kumArikA, dArikA.
LASS , s. taruRI, kumArI, kanyA, bAlA -likA, dArikA, putrI.
Lassitude, s. KedaH, klamaH, glAni f.; See Languidness.
LASSITUDE: (1) glAniH: v. Languor;(2) tandrA: v. Sloth.

LASSITUDE , s. glAniH f., glAnatA, avasAdaH, sAdaH, avasannatA, vizAdaH, vizaRRatA, tandrA -ndrI -ndrikA -ndriH f., KedaH, pramIlA, aNgaSETilyaM, aNgaSiTilatA, mandatA, mAndyaM, klAntiH f., klAntatA, mlAniH f., SrAntiH f., pariSrAntiH, klamaH.
Lasso, s. pASaH, pASabaMDaH-rajju f.
LASSO , s. pASaH, pASarajjuH m. f., pASabanDaH, vAgurA.

Last, a. aMtya, aMtima, avara, avatarama, carama, paScima; Seza-aMta- in comp. 2 gata, atIta, carama, pUrva, BUta. 3 jaGanya, aDama, apakfzwa. 4 parama, uttama, atyaMta; ‘l(ast) night’ gatAyAM rAtrO; ‘the l(ast) year’ gata-atIta-saMvatsaraH, parut ind.; ‘l(ast) but one’ upAMtya, upAMtika; ‘l(ast)-born’ avaraja; ‘at l(ast)’ ate, aMtataH; ‘l(ast) part’ SezaBAgaH; ‘l(ast) part of the night’ uttararAtraH, caramayAmaH; ‘l(ast) half’ uttarArDaH, paScArDaH, parArDaH, ‘the year before l(ast)’ parAri ind.; ‘to the l(ast)’ SezaM yAvat. adv. aMte, Seze, aMtataH, avaraM, caramaM, avarataH. v. i. avasTA 1 A, sTA 1 P; oft. by avaDiH in comp.; ‘l(ast)ing for many days’ cirasTAyin, eza te jI-vitAvaDiH pravAdaH (U. 1) ‘will l(ast) through life’; ‘this will l(ast) as food for four months’ etena (asmAkaM) mAsacatuzwayasya BojanaM Bavizyati; ‘the bloom of youth l(ast)s for a few days’ katipayadivasasTAyinI yOvanaSrIH (Bh. ii. 2). [Last]ing, a. sTAyin, cira-dIrGa-kAlasTAyin; anapAyin, nitya, sTira, Druva, akzaya, SASvata (tI f.), ajara, ciraMtana (nI f.). [Last]ly, adv. aMte, aMtataH, caramataH, Seze, avarataH.
LAST (subs.): *mUlapAdukA; pAdukAliNgam.

LAST (adj.): I Final:(1) antya (f. ntyA) or anta- in comp., l. syllable antyAkzaram; to the l.: antaparyantam; at l.: ante [Seze or avaSeze is used in this sense in Bengali, but I do not remem- -ber any instance in Sanskrit];(2) caramaH (mA, maM), nor the l.: nApi caramaH, D.s.;(3) paScimaH (mA, maM), getting up at the l. watch: yAma utTAya paScime, Mah.; l. order of (their) master: martuH paScimAjYA, R. xvii. 8.II Preceding:(1) pUrvaH (rvA, rvaM) (= former);(2) gataH (tA, taM) (= past), l. year: gatavarzaH. Ph.: l. evening: hyaH pradoze: v. Yesterday.
LAST (adv.): v. Lastly, l. -born: jaGanyajaH (jA, jaM) (rare).
LAST (v.): tizWati (sTA, c. 1.), l. s one moment: tizWatyekakzaRam, V ii. 1.; l. ing but one moment: kzaRamAtrasTAyin (f. nI), M. n.: v. To remain.

LAST , a. (Final) antimaH -mA -maM, antyaH -ntyA -ntyaM, anta in comp., Seza in comp., avaraH -rA -raM, caramaH -mA -maM, avaratamaH -mA -maM. — (Hindmost) paScimaH -mA -maM, jaGanyaH -nyA -nyaM, avaraH -rA -raM, pAScAtyaH -tyA -tyaM, paScAtIyaH -yA -yaM. — (Next before the present) gataH -tA -taM, atItaH -tA -taM, BUtaH -tA -taM. — (Last but one) upAntaH -ntA -ntaM, upAntikaH -kI -kaM, upAntyaH -ntyA -ntyaM. — (Extreme) paramaH -mA -maM, atyantaH -ntA -ntaM, AtyantikaH -kI -kaM, uttamaH -mA -maM. — (Lowest) aDamaH -mA -maM, avaraH -rA -raM, aDaraH -rA -raM, avamaH -mA -maM, apakfzwaH -zwA -zwaM; ‘come last,’ avarAgataH -tA -taM, caramAgataH -tA -taM; ‘born last,’ avarajaH -jA -jaM, jaGanyajaH -jA -jaM; ‘last state,’ SezAvasTA, SezadaSA, pariRAmaH; ‘last past,’ SezaBAgaH; ‘last part of the night,’ SezarAtriH f.; ‘last half,’ avarArdDaM, paScArdDaM; ‘last night,’ gatarAtriH f.; ‘last month,’ gatamAsaH; ‘last year,’ gatavatsaraH, parut; ‘belonging to last year,’ parutnaH -tnA -tnaM; ‘year before last,’ parAri; ‘belonging to the year before last,’ parAritnaH -tnA -tnaM; ‘at last,’ Seze, ante, Sezatas, avaSeze, antatas, anantaraM, cirakAlAtparaM, dIrGakAlAtparaM, caramaM; ‘to the last,’ SezaM yAvat.
LAST , adv. avaraM, caramaM, antatas, ante, Sezatas, paScAt, avarastAt, avastAt; ‘come last,’ avarAgataH -tA -taM, caramAgataH -tA -taM; ‘born last,’ avarajaH -jA -jaM, jaGanyajaH -jA -jaM.
LAST , s. (Of a shoe) kAzWamayaH pAdukAsaMskAraH or pAdukAkAraH.
To LAST , v. n. sTA (c. 1. tizWati -te, sTAtuM), saMsTA, paryavasTA, sTirIBU, cirasTAyI -yinI -yi BU.
LAST-MENTIONED , a. uttaroktaH -ktA -ktaM, aparoktaH -ktA -ktaM, avaroktaH -ktA -ktaM.
LASTING (adj.): (1) sTAyin (f. nI);(2) sTAsnu (mfn.), l. fame: sTAsnu yaSaH, Ki. ii. 19.;(3) cirasTAyin (f. nI) (= l. long).

LASTING , a. sTAyI -yinI -yi (n), cirasTAyI &c., dIrGakAlasTAyI &c., cirakAlasTAyI &c., cirakAlikaH -kA -kaM, sTiraH -rA -raM, sTAvaraH -rA -raM, saMsTaH -sTA -sTaM, sTitimAn -matI -mat (t), anapAyI -yinI -yi (n), nityasTAyI &c., nityaH -tyA -tyaM, DruvaH -vA -vaM, SASvataH -tI -taM, avisargI -rgiRI -rgi (n), ajaraH -rA -raM, akzayaH -yA -yaM, cirantanaH -nI -naM.
LASTINGNESS , s. sTAyitvaM, cirasTAyitvaM, sTiratA, sTitiH f., saMsTitiH f., sTAvaratvaM, nityatA, ajaratvaM, anapAyaH, DruvatA, DrOvyaM.
LASTLY: (1) caramam or caramataH;(2) paScimataH (rare); (3) antataH (?).
LASTLY , adv. antatas, ante, Sezatas, Seze, avaSeze -zatas, avarastAt.
Latch, s. argalA-laM, vizkaMBaH, argalAbaMDaH, tAlakaM, dvArabaMDanI; ‘the postern door was on the l(atch)’ argalAnirudDaM pakzadvAraM.
LATCH: KillaH (?); argalaH (= bolt).
LATCH , s. tAlakaM, tAlaH, tAlayantraM, argalaH -lA -lI, kIlaH, kapAwaba- nDanI, dvArabanDanI, dvArayantraM.
To LATCH , v. a. tAlakAdinA dvAraM banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM).
Latchet, s. pAdukAbaMDanI.
LATCHET: of a shoe: sUtram (??); banDanI (??).
LATCHET , s. pAdukAbanDanaM -nI, pAdukAbanDaH, pAdukAyoktraM.

Late, a. vilaMbena Agata or prApta; kAlAtIta, velAtIta, samayAtIta, atikrAMtakAla, ati-kAla, atItakAla-samaya. 2 avasita, pariRata, avasanna. 3 nUtana, acira, pratyagra, aBinava, ADunika (kI f.), nAtipurARa, sadyaskA-lIna. 4 atIta, gaMta, vyatIta, BUta; prAktana-pUrvatana (nI f.), pOrvika (kI f.), ‘at a l(ate) hour of the day’ pariRate divase, avasannaprAye ahani; ‘at a l(ate) hour of the night’ kzIRaBUyizWAyAM kzapAyAM; ‘at a l(ate) period of life’ pariRate vayasi. adv. vilaMbena, vilaMbAt, velAtikrameRa, atikAlaM-samayaM, cireRa, cirAt, cirakAlena-lAt; ‘to be l(ate)’ velAtikramaM kf 8 U, cira(rA)yati (D.); ‘why are you l(ate)’ kimiti cirA-yita tvayA; ‘l(ate) in life’ pariRatavayasi; See above; ‘too l(ate) in the day’ atiparAhRe; ‘too l(ate) in the evening’ atisAye. 2 akAle, asamaye. [Late]ly, ‘of late’, adv. idAnIMtane kAle, nAticirAtprAk, ADunika-samaye; aciraM. [Late]ness, s. kAlAtItatA, kA-lAtikramaH; pariRAmaH, pariRati f. Later, a. uttara, apara, para, uttarakAlIna, pAScAtya. adv. (on) uttaraM, uttarottaraM, paScAt, uttara-para-kAle.

LATE (adj.): I Long delayed: expr. with vilambena or cireRa, the summer is l. this year: *asmin varze cireRAgato nidAGaH.II Far advanced: pariRataH (tA, taM), l. in the day: pariRate divase. Ph.: at l. hours (of night): akAle or (?) riraMsAkAle, D. III Departed, out of office: pUrvatanaH (nI, naM). IV Not long past: expr. with itaH kiYcit pUrzam, L. p.:(1) paraH (rA, raM);(2) aDastanaH (nI, naM) (of persons or things in position), l. r than the works. granTAnAmaDastanaH, Mahesha.: v. Deceased: q. v.

LATE (adv.): I At an advanced time:(1) vilambena;(2) cireRa. Ph.: sooner or l. r: adya Svo vA; too l.: atItakAlaH (lA, laM), vi-, R. v. 14. II Lately: q. v.III Far in the night: akAle or asamaye. Ph.: of l.: aDunAtanakAle;(2) idAnIntanakAle;(3) aDunA- (= now: in connec- -tion with formerly).

LATE , a. (After the usual time, tardy) kAlAtItaH -tA -taM, samayA- tItaH -tA -taM, atItakAlaH -lA -laM, kAlAtikrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, atikrA- ntakAlaH -lA -laM, velAtItaH -tA -taM, vilambAgataH -tA -taM, vilambenAgataH -tA -taM, vilambitaH -tA -taM, mandaH -ndA -ndaM, cirakAlInaH -nA -naM, cirakAlAdAgataH -tA -taM, atikAlaH -lA -laM. — (Far advanced towards the close) avasannaH -nnA -nnaM, avasitaH -tA -taM, pariRataH -tA -taM; ‘at a late hour of the day,’ avasanne divase, aparAhle, parAhle; ‘at a late hour of the night,’ avasannAyAM rAtrO, apara- rAtrO, rAtrimaDye, SezarAtrO; ‘at a late period of life,’ pariRate vayasi. — (Ripening after the time) niyamitakAlAt paraM or upayuktakAlAt paraM pakvaH -kvA -kvaM or pariRataH -tA -taM. — (Recent) nUtanaH -nA -naM, navaH -vA -vaM, aBinavaH -vA -vaM, aciraH -rA -raM, ADunikaH -kI -kaM, aDunAtanaH -nI -naM, idAnIntanaH -nI -naM, sadyaskaH -skA -skaM, sadyaskAlInaH -nA -naM, arvvAcInaH -nA -naM, aprAcInaH -nA -naM, pratyagraH -grA -graM, varttamAnakAlInaH -nA -naM, avyavahitadIrGakAlaH -lA -laM. — (Past, gone) atItaH -tA -taM, vyatItaH -tA -taM, gataH -tA -taM, BUtaH -tA -taM. — (Former) prAktanaH -nI -naM, pUrvvatanaH -nI -naM, pOrvvikaH -kI -kaM.

LATE , adv. (After the usual time, after delay) vilambena, vilambAt, cirakAle -lAt, atikAlaM, atisamayaM, atItakAlaM, mandaM, vilambitaM, cirAt -reRa; ‘come late,’ vilambAgataH -tA -taM, vilambenAgataH &c., cirAdAgataH &c., cirakAlAdAgataH &c.; ‘ripening late,’ upayukta- kAlAt paraM pakvaH -kvA -kvaM; ‘late at night,’ avasannAyAM rAtrO, rAtrimaDye, maDyarAtraM, apararAtraM, mahAniSAyAM; ‘late in the day,’ aparAhle, parAhle, avasanne divase; ‘late in life,’ pariRate vayasi. — (Not long ago, recently) nUtanaM, avyavahitadIrGakAle, avyavahita- pUrvvakAle; ‘too late in the evening,’ atisAye; ‘too late in the day,’ atiparAhle; ‘too late in life,’ atipariRatavayasi, supariRatavayasi.
LATEEN , s. latInnAmA triBujAkAro vAtavasanaviSezaH.
LATELY: (1) idAnImeva (?);(2) kiYcitpUrvam.
LATELY , adv. avyavahitadIrGakAle, avyavahitapUrvvakAle, nUtanaM, arvAk, arvAkkAle, nUtanakAle, sadyaskAle, aDunAtanakAle, idAnIntanakAle, apurA, aprAkkAle, pratyagraM.
LATENESS , s. kAlAtItatA, atItakAlatvaM, kAlAtikrAntatA, atikAlatA, cirakAlInatA, kAlAtikramaH, pariRatiH f., pariRAmaH.
Latent, a. ni-, lIna, gUQa, Canna, gupta, adfzwa, apratyakza, aprakASa, aprakawa, adfSya, aMtarhita, niBfta; ‘a l(atent) disease’ DAtusTaH-SarIrAMtargataH-rogaH.
LATENT: nigUQaH (QA, QaM): v. Hidden, invisible.

LATENT , a. gUQaH -QA -QaM, guptaH -ptA -ptaM, nigUQaH -QA -QaM, CannaH -nnA -nnaM, pracCannaH -nnA -nnaM, adfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, adfSyaH -SyA -SyaM, guhyaH -hyA -hyaM, niBftaH -tA -taM, rahasyaH -syA -syaM, antarhitaH -tA -taM, apratyakzaH -kzA -kzaM, aprakawaH -wA -waM, aprakASaH -SA -SaM; ‘as a disease,’ majjAgataH -tA -taM, DAtusTaH -sTA -sTaM.
LATER , a. uttaraH -rA -raM, paraH -rA -raM, avaraH -rA -raM, pAScAtyaH -tyA -tyaM.
Lateral, a. pArSvIya, pArSvasTa, pArSvika (kI f.). [Lateral]ly, adv. pArSvaBAge, pArSvataH, pArSve.
LATERAL: (1) by comp.: v. Side;(2) pArSvikaH (kA, kaM).
LATERAL , a. pArSvikaH -kI -kaM, pArSvIyaH -yA -yaM, pArSvaH -rSvA -rSvaM, pArSva- tIyaH -yA -yaM, anupArSvaH -rSvA -rSvaM, pArSvasTaH -sTA -sTaM, pArSvasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
LATERALLY: pArSvataH: v. Sidewise.
LATERALLY , adv. pArSvatas, pArSve, anupArSvaM, pArSvaBAge, pArSvadiSi.
Lath, s. sUkzmakAzWaM-dAru, tanuPalakaH-kaM.
LATH: sUkzmaPalakaH, Monier Williams.
LATH , s. sUkzmaPalakaH -kaM, sUkzmakAzWaM, sUkzmadAruH m., dIrGakAzWaM, dIrGaPalakaH -kaM, tanuPalakaH -kaM, kAzWaPalakaH.
To LATH , v. a. sUkzmaPalakEr Avf (c. 5. -vfRoti -varitu -rItuM) or AstF (c. 9. -stfRAti -starituM -rItuM), Palaka (nom. Palakayati -yituM).
Lathe, s. kuMdaH-daM, BramaH-mi f., cakraM.
LATHE: (1) kundaH;(2) mramiH (maH).
LATHE , s. BramaH, BramiH f., kundaH, cakraM, cakrayantraM, yantrakaH.
Lather, s. aMjanaPenaH, mArjanatElaPenaH.
LATHER: (subs.) PenaH (the exact sense being determined by context): v. Foam.
LATHER (v.): PenAyate: v. To froth.
LATHER , s. aYjanaPenaH, aByaYjanaPenaH, mArjanatElaPenaH, mArjanalepaPenaH.
To LATHER , v. a. aYjanaPenena lip (c. 6. limpati, leptuM), PenaliptaM -ptAM kf.
To LATHER , v. n. Pena (nom. PenAyate -yituM), PenalaH -lA -laM BU.
LATHY , a. kAzWaPalakavat tanuH -nuH -nvI -nu, sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM.
Latifolious, a. pfTu-viSAla-parRa.
LATIFOLIOUS , a. pfTupatraH -trA -traM, pfTuparRaH -rRA -rRaM.
LATIN , s. (The language) lAtinAKyA BAzA, lAtinBAzA.
LATINISM , s. lAtinBAzAnusAriRI vAgvfttiH, lAtinBAzAsampradAyaH.
LATINIST: *lAwinamAzABijYaH, -viSAradaH, etc.
LATINITY: *viSudDalAwinam; lAwinam will often do.
LATINITY , s. lAtinBAzAyAH SudDatA or viSudDiH f.
LATITANCY , s. guptatA, gUQatA, guptaBAvaH, pracCannatA, aprakASatA.
LATITANT , a. guptaH -ptA -ptaM, gUQaH -QA -QaM, pracCannaH -nnA -nnaM, niBftaH -tA -taM.

Latitude, s. akzaH. 2 (Celestial) nikzepaH. 3 vistAraH, vistfti f., praTiman m., Ayati f. 4 aniyaMtraRaM, svAtaMtryaM, niyamopekzA, niya-mAtikramaH, SETilyaM; ‘degree of l(atitude)’ akzAMSaH; ‘l(atitude) of a planet’ patanaM; ‘parallel of l(atitude)’ akzAMSavfttaM. Latitudinarian, a. SiTila, aniyaMtraRa, niryaMtraRa. s. matasvAtaMtryAvalaM-bin m., nirbaMDahInaH. [Latitudinarian]ism, s. mataSETilyaM, vicArasvAtaMtryaM, aniyaMtraRaM.

LATITUDE: I Geo.: akzAMSaH, Su. com.; akza- BAgaH, Gan. Ph.: place of no. l.: nirakzadeSaH; they have no l.: tAsu nAkzasyonnatirazyate, Su. xii. 42.; celestial l: vikzepaH, Su.II Breadth: q. v.III Laxity, freedom: gurulAGavam (??).

LATITUDE , s. (Terrestrial) akzaH, PalaH, vizuvavfttAntaraM, vizuvareKAntaraM. — (Celestial) vikzepaH, SaraH; ‘a degree of latitude,’ akzaBAgaH, akzAMSaH; ‘opposite degrees of latitude,’ anupAtaH; ‘latitude of a planet,’ patanaM; ‘argument of latitude,’ akzakarRaH; ‘circle or parallel of latitude,’ akzavfttaM, akzAMSavfttaM, svadeSapa- riDiH m., svadeSamaDyapariDiH m.; ‘having no latitude,’ nirakzaH -kzA -kzaM. — (Breadth) pfTutA, praTimA m. (n), vistftiH f., prasTaH. — (Laxity) SETilyaM, SiTilatA -tvaM, anirbanDaH, nirbanDahInatA, niyamA- tikramaH, niyamopekzA, aDftiH f.
LATITUDINAL: expr. by comp., l. difference: akzaBedaH.
LATITUDINAL , a. anuprasTaH -sTA -sTaM, anvAyatanaH -nA -naM, akzIyaH -yA -yaM.
LATITUDINARIAN: *SiTilaGarmaBaktaH (ktA, ktaM).

LATITUDINARIAN , a. SiTilaH -lA -laM, nirbanDahInaH -nA -naM, aDfti- mAn -matI -mat (t), SAstraSETilyAnuyAyI -yinI -yi (n), niyamA- tikramI -miRI -mi (n), niyamopekzakaH -kA -kaM, mataSETilyAvalambI -mbinI -mbi (n), SiTilabudDiH -dDiH -dDi.
LATITUDINARIANISM: *SiTilaDarmaBaktiH.
LATITUDINARIANISM , s. mataSETilyaM, SETilyaM, SiTilatA -tvaM, SiTila- budDitvaM, anirbanDaH, nirbanDahInatA, niyamAtikramaH, nirbanDopakzA, aDftiH f.
LATRANT , a. BazakaH -kA -kaM, rAvI -viRI -vi (n), rutakArI &c.
LATROCINY , s. steyaM, cOryyaM, stEnyaM. See LARCENY.
Latten, s. rIti f., pittalaM.
LATTEN , s. kAMsyaM, rItiH f., pittalaM. — (Sheet tin) trapupatraM.

Latter, a. uttara, apara, para, avara, anya, (pron. a.); paScima, carama, aMtima; utta-rokta, aparokta; ‘former and l(atter)’ pUrvAparaM; ‘in the l(atter) part of the day’ parAhRe. [Latter]ly, adv. arvAkkAle, aDunAtanakAle; See Lately.
LATTER (adj.): uttaraH (rA, raM) (in all the senses): v. Former, subsequent.

LATTER , a. LAWFULLY: viDyanusAreRa (?); nyAyataH (= justly).

LAWFULLY , adv. DarmmeRa, Darmmatas, DarmmAnusAreRa -rAt, DarmmaSAstrAnusAreRa, smftiSAstrAnusAreRa, vyavahAraviDyanusAreRa, vyavasTAnurUpeRa, rAjyaniya- mAnurUpeRa, nyAyatas, nyAyAnusAreRa, yaTAnyAyaM, nyAyyaM.
LAWFULNESS: (1) vEDatA (?).:(2) nyAyyatA (= justness).
LAWFULNESS , s. DarmyatvaM, DarmmAnusAritvaM, DarmmAnusAraH, DarmmaSAstrAnusAritA, smftiSAstrAnuyAyitA, DarmmaSAstrAnukUlyaM, nyAyAnusAraH -ritA, nyAyyatvaM.
LAWGIVER: viDipravartakaH (?); smftikAraH (only of the Smritis).

LAWLESS: I Lit.: avEDaH (DI, DaM) (?).II Un- -restrained: aniyantraRa (f. RA).

LAWLESSLY , adv. DarmmaviroDena, smftiviroDena, vyavahAravirudDaM, AcAravi- roDena, durAcAravat, DarmmaBrazwavat, aSizwavat, avaSaM, ucCfNKalaM.
LAWLESSNESS: I Lit.: avEDatA.II Fig.: aniyantraRA.

LAX (adj.): I Loose: q. v.: SiTilaH (lA, laM). II Not strict: SiTilaH (lA, laM) (?); mfdu (f. dvI) (= gentle).III Of the bowel: SiTilaH (lA, laM).

LAX , a. (Loose) SiTilaH -lA -laM, SlaTaH -TA -TaM, praSlaTaH -TA -TaM, viga- litaH -tA -taM, srastaH -stA -staM, abadDaH -dDA -dDaM. — (In morals) anavasTaH -sTA -sTaM, durAcAraH -rA -raM, anAcArI -riRI -ri (n), DarmmaBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, karmmaBrazwaH &c., vyaBicArI &c. — (In the bowels) mfdukozWaH -zWA -zWaM, abadDakozWaH -zWA -zWaM. — (In discipline) atIkzRadaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, SiTiladaRqaH -RqA -RqaM.
LAX , s. (Diarrhœa) sAraRaH, atisAraH, pravAhikA, virekaH.

LAXITY: SETilyam: v. Looseness.

LAXLY: SiTilam: v. Loosely.
LAXNESS: SiTilatA: v. Looseness.

Lay, v. t. DA 3 U, ni-A°, nyas 4 U, ni-viS c., sTA c. (sTApayati); sam-f c. (arpayati), nikzip 6 P, Aruh c. [Lay] down, nyas, nikzip, ni-DA, nyAsIkf. 2 SI c., niviS c. 3 vimuc, pari-, tyaj, vi-hA. 4 (Oneself) saMviS 6 P, SI 2 A. 5 pra-RI 1 P, vi-DA (rules &c.); ‘l(ay) down arms’ yudDAdviram 1 P, Sa-raRaM vraj 1 P; ‘l(ay) down life’ prARAn tyaj. [Lay] out, vini-yuj 7 A, 10, pra-yuj, vyay 10 (vyayayati). 2 pari-pra-kxp c., vi-nyas 4 U, virac 10, pra-yuj, ciMt 10; See Contrive. 3 prasf c., vistF c., dIrGIkf; prakAS c., prakawIkf ‘l(ay) oneself out’; cezw 1 A, prayat 1 A, udyam 1 A. [Lay] to, A-ruh c., nikzip; See Ascribe; ‘l(ay) to a ship’ nOgatiM ruD or staMB. [Lay] up, ni-DA, rakz, saMci; ‘to be laid up’, SayyAgrasta a. BU 1 P, utTAtuM akzama a. BU; ‘laid up with fever’ jvareRotTAtumakzamaH. Lay, s. gAnaM, gItaM, kAvyaM. 2 AstaraH-raRaM, PalakaH-kaM. a. sAmAnya, sADAraRa (RI f.), purohitaBinna. [Lay]man, s. gfhasTaH, sAmAnya-sADAraRa-janaH, adIkzitaH, prAkftaH. Laical, a. gfhasTin, gArhasTika (kI f.), purohitaBinna, adIkzita. Laity, s. gfhasTa-sAmAnya-janavargaH, prAkfta-sADAraRa-janAH, purohitaBinnavargaH.

LAY (v.): I To place, put: q. v.: nidaDAti [Page410] (DA, c. 3.).II To cause to lie: SAyayati (c. of SI) (rare): v. To lie.III To fell: q. v.: pAtayati (c. of pat).IV Miscell.: to l. dust: rajaH Samayati, Ki. vi. 27.; to l. eggs: aRqaka- vimokzaRaM karoti, P. (H. has prasUte, not aRqAni prasUte: qimbAn dadAti is used in the vernacular); to l. a snare: unmATaM prayojayati, Mah.; to l. com- mand: SAsanaM prayojayati; to l. paint, etc: raNgaM, etc. dadAti; to l. siege: roDaM karoti, (with gen.); “when the winds are laid”: SAnte vAte; l. blame upon: dozam Aropayati (c. of ruh) (with loc.); to l. waste: KilIkaroti: v. To devastate; to l. a tax, etc.: karaM, etc. sTApayati (c. of sTA).
LAY (subs.): I A song: q. v.: gItam.II A meadow: BUmiH.III A layer: staraH.

To LAY , v. a. (Place, set) DA (c. 3. daDAti, DAtuM), niDA, ADA, nyas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM), sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM), niviS (c. 10. -veSayati -yituM), Aruh in caus. (-ropayati -yituM), f in caus. (arpa- yati -yituM), dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM), Df (c. 1. Darati, DarttuM), kf; ‘he lays the cup on the ground,’ pAtraM BUmO nidaDAti or nyasyati; ‘he lays the goat on his shoulders,’ CAgaM skanDe or skanDena karoti; ‘lay your hand on my shoulder,’ matskanDe hastaM dehi. — (Place in order) vinyas, viDA, saMviDA, prativiDA, virac (c. 10. -racayati -yituM), krameRa sTA. — (Beat down) pat (c. 10. pAtayati -yituM), nipat. — (Spread) AstF (c. 9. -stfRAti, c. 5. -stfRoti -starituM -rItuM), vistF; ‘to lay snares,’ jAlaM vistF; ‘he lays sacred grass over the ground,’ BUmiM kuSEr AstfRAti. — (Spread on a surface) lip (c. 6. -limpati, leptuM) with acc. and instr. c. — (Still, quiet, calm) Sam (c. 10. Samayati -yituM), praSam, upaSam, sAntv or SAntv (c. 10. sAntvayati -yituM), aBiSAntv, pariSAntv. — (Lay a wager) paR (c. 1. paRate -RituM), vipaR, nikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM), paRaM kf, pratijYAM kf. — (Lay eggs) aRqAni su (c. 2. sUte, c. 4. sUyate, sotuM) or prasu. — (Lay the blame) kasmiMScid dozam Aruh or kzip, dozAropaRa kf, dozaprasaNgaM kf. — (Apply) ADA, nyas, saMyuj (c. 10. -yojayati -yituM), f in caus. — (Impose) nyas, niviS, niyuj, Aruh in caus. — (Lay a command) AdeSaM kf, AjYAM kf, jiyuj. — (Lay an ambush) parAkramaRArTaM sEnyam niBfte sTA in caus. — (Lay a plot, scheme) kapawaprabanDaM kf, saNkalpaM kf, upAyaM pracint (c. 10. -cintayati -yituM) or Gaw (c. 1. Gawate -wituM) or viDA or prayuj. — (Lay siege) parivezw (c. 1. -vezwata -zwituM), ruD (c. 7. ruRadDi, rodDuM), avaruD, uparuD. — (Lay waste) upadru (c. 1. -dravati -drotuM), upaplu (c. 1. -plavate -plotuM), bAD (c. 1. bADate -DituM), prabAD, paribAD, nirdah (c. 1. -dahati -dagDuM), dah, nirjanIkf. — (Lay aside) nyas, sannyas, tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM), parityaj, santyaj, hA (c. 3. jahAti, hAtuM), apahA, utsfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), ujJ (c. 6. ujJati -jJituM), projJ, avahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), avamuc (c. 6. -muYcati -moktuM); ‘one who has laid aside his anger,’ astakopaH -pA -paM. — (Lay before) prasf (c. 10. -sAra- yati -yituM), nivid (c. 10. -vedayati -yituM), upanyas, f in caus. — (Lay by) sannyas, parirakz (c. 1. -rakzati -kzituM), rakz, niDA, niDiM kf; ‘he lays by the food left by the crows,’ kAkeByaH SizwaM mAMsaM rakzati. — (Lay down, deposit) nyas, upanyas, pratinyas, nikzip,
To LAY , v. n. (Produce eggs) aRqAni su (c. 2. sUte, c. 4. sUyate, sotuM) or prasu or jan (c. 10. janayati -yituM) or prajan (c. 4. -jAyate -janituM) or utpad (c. 10. -pAdayati -yituM).
LAY , s. (Stratum, layer) staraH, AstaraRaM, AstaraH, PalakaH -kaM, puwaH. — (Song) gItaM, gAnaM, kavitA, kAvyaM.

LAY , a. (Not clerical) gfhasTavargasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), gfhasTI -sTinI -sTi (n), gArhasTikaH -kI -kaM, purohitavargaBinnaH -nnA -nnaM, pOrohityaBinnaH -nnA -nnaM, DarmmapadasTaBinnaH -nnA -nnaM, DarmmapadasTAtiriktaH -ktA -ktaM, sAmAnyalokasambanDI &c., sADAraRalokasambanDI &c., DarmmADikAra- dIkzAhInaH -nA -naM, ajAtaDarmmADikAradIkzaH -kzA -kzaM.
LAY , a. vyavahArikaH -kI -kaM. LAYMAN, vyavahArI m.

LAY ASIDE: I Not to retain:(1) apa-asyati, nir- (as, c. 4.), how all that was suddenly l. d a: sarvaM tadekapadameva kaTaM nirastam, Vi. iii. 13.;(2) vimuYcati (muc, c. 6.) (= to leave: q. v.), l. ing a. (her) necklace: hAraM vimucya, Ku. v. 8.II To reserve: q. v.:
LAY BEFORE: upanyasyati (as, c. 4.) (?).
LAY BY: rakzati (rakz, c. 1.): v. To keep, reserve.
LAY DOWN: I To abandon: q. v.: muYcati, vi-, (muc, c. 6.), l. d d. arms: SastrARi mumoca, Ki. ii. 9. II To determine, decide: q. v.: nirDArayati (Df, c. 10.).

LAY TO: I To impute: q. v.II Of ships: gatiroDaM karoti.
LAY TOGETHER: samAharati (hf, c. 1.): v. To collect. Ph.: l. heads: ekatra mantrayati, (mantr, c. 10.).
LAY UP: I To store, l. in: q. v.: saMcinoti (ci, c. 5.).II In pass., confined to bed: utTAtuM akzamaH (mA, maM): v. Also bed.
LAY UPON: i. e. to wager: q. v.: paRyatAM nayati (nI, c. 1.), Ki.
LAY WAIT FOR: kramaM kftvA niBftaM tizWati (sTA, c. 1.), P.
LAY-FIGURE , s. citrakarmmaRi prayuktA kAzWanirmmitA puruzAkArA mUrttiH.

Layer, s. staraH; AstaraH-raRaM, PalakaH-kaM. 2 Twig, q. v.

Lead, s. sIsaM, sIsakaM, nAgaM, yogezwaM, vapraM; ‘red l(ead)’ siMdUraM, nAgasaMBavaM, raktacUrRaM, nAgajaM, nAgagarBaM. s. nAyakatvaM, netftvaM, aDizWAtftvaM, muKyatvaM, agragamanaM-yAnaM, puraHsaraRaM. v. t. nI 1 P, vah 1 P, prAp c., gam c. (gamayati) (all with two accusatives); A-dA 3 A. 2 (Way) dfS c., A-nir-diS 6 P. 3 aDi-zWA 1 P, aDyAs 2 A, praRI, A-nir-diS; puraskf 8 U, agraRIH-nAyakaH-agresaraH-BU 1 P (with gen.); vasizWADizWitA devyaH (U. 1) ‘led by Vasishtha’ &c., daSaraTasya dArAnaDi-zWAya (U. 4) ‘led by the demon’ dAnavaM puraskftya. 4 Akfz 1 P, pra-vi-luB c., pra-vft c. prer c., protsah c. nI; mUQaH parapratyaya-neyabudDiH (M. 1) ‘has his mind led by the convictions of others’. 5 (Time) nI, gam c., ativah c., kzE c. (kzapayati), yA c. (yApayati); ‘led a dissolute life’ vizayasuKanirato jI-vitamatyavAhayat; ‘l(ead)ing a life above their station’ svasTAnAnucitAM-svasTAnA-tiriktAM-jIvayAtrAM kalpayaMtaH. v. i. (janayati); ‘advice to fools l(ead)s to their provocation’ upadeSo hi mUrKARAM prakopAya (Bavati) (H. 3). [Lead]ed, sIsakayukta. [Lead]en, a. sIsakanirmita. Led, a. nIta, prerita, aDizWita, &c.; ‘l(ed) by’ ex. by puraHsara, purogama, pramuKa, Adi in comp.
LEAD (subs.): I The metal: sIsam, -kam, Bha. Red l. powder: sindUram.II Precedence: expr. by adj. or verb, to take the l.: agrato yAti, H.

LEAD (v. t.): I To guide:(1) nayati (nI, c. 1.) (= to conduct: q. v.);(2) AdiSati (diS, c. 6 (with gen.) or AdeSayati (c. of diS) (in showing), l. me the way: AdiSatu me mArgam,V ii. Ph.: with the hand led the daughter of the Chief Mountain to the marriage chamber: kzitiDarapatikanyAmAdadAnaH kareRa.....kOtukAgAramAgAt, Ku. vii. 94.; led by her finger: tvadIyAmaNgulimava- lambya, R. iii. 25.; l. to success: sidDiM nayati, Ki. II To command: q. v.: aDitizWati (sTA, c. l.). Ph.: led by whom: yaM puraskftya, Ku. ii. 52.III To go before: puro gacCati (gam, c. l.), etc. (with gen.).IV To pass, [Page411] spend: q. v.: nayati: v. To influence: harati (hf, c. 1.).
LEAD (v. t.): I To go before: puro Bavati, etc. Ku. xiii. 11.II To tend: the road l. ing to the Golden City: suvarRapuragAmI panTAH, Ku. poverty l. s to shame: dAridryAdDiyameti, Mr. i.

LEAD , s. (The metal) sIsaM, sIsakaM, sIsapatrakaM, nAgaM, vapraM, yogezwaM, trapuH n., trapus n., vaNgaM, kuvaNgaM, piccawaM, SirAvfttaM, tamaraM, jaqaM, cInaM, bahumalaM, yAmunezWakaM, paripizwakaM, sindUrakAraRaM, tAraSudDikaraM; ‘red-lead,’ sindUraM -rikA, nAgasamBavaM, nAgajaM, nAgaraktaH, nAgagarBaH, SoRaM, sOBAgyaM, raktacUrRaM, raktabAlukaM, raktareRaH m., SfNgAraM, SfNgAraBUzaRaM; ‘marked with red-lead,’ sindUratilakaH -kA -kaM. — (Plummet) lambaH -mbakaH, lambasIsakaM.

(yApayati -yituM) or gam in caus. — (Lead forth, lead up) unnI, utkfz, prakfz, udgam in caus. — (Lead back) pratyAnI, nivft in caus.

LEAN (v.): I To 1. on or upon: avalambate (lamb, c. 1 (with acc.).II To be dis- -posed: pravaRa (f. RA).III To bend, deviate: namati, ava-, (nam, c. 1.).

To LEAN , v. n. (Incline, bend) nam (c. 1. namati, nantuM), avanam, Anam, namrIBU. — (Bend out of the perpendicular) vahirlamb (c. 1. -lambate -mbituM), vahiHpralamb, tiryyak pralamb, vakrIBU. — (Lean on, rest on) avalamb, samAlamb, avalambanaM kf, saMSri (c. 1. -Srayati -te -yituM), samASri, upASri, nilI (c. 4. -lIyate -letuM); ‘she leans on the arms of Rāma,’ ezA rAmasya bAhU saMSrayati or avalambate.

LEAN , a. (Thin, meagre) kfSaH -SA -SaM, parikfSaH -SA -SaM, kfSANgaH -NgI -NgaM, kzIRaSarIraH -rA -raM, kzIRamAMsaH -sA -saM, amAMsaH -sA -saM, SuzkamAMsaH -sA -saM, kzIRaH -RA -RaM, apuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, vipuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, tanuH -nuH -nvI -nu, pratanuH &c., vitanuH &c., kzAmaH -mA -maM, SIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, SAtaH -tA -taM, SuzkANgaH -NgI -NgaM.
LEAN , s. (That part of the flesh which consists of muscle without the fat) snAyuH m., snasA, mAMsasnAyuH, mAMsaM, medoBinnaH or vasABinno mAMsaBAgaH.
LEAN-FACED , a. kfSamuKaH -KI -KaM, kzIRamuKaH &c., kzIRavadanaH -nA -naM.

LEANING , part. or a. (Bending, deviating from the straight line) praRataH -tA -taM, AnataH -tA -taM, pravaRaH -RA -RaM, vahirlambaH -mbA -mbaM, pralambaH -mbA -mbaM, namraH -mrA -mraM, vakraH -krA -kraM. — (Resting on) avalambI -mbinI -mbi (n), avalambanaH -nA -naM, avalambitaH -tA -taM, saMSritaH -tA -taM, samASritaH -tA -taM, upASritaH -tA -taM.
LEANNESS: (1) kfSatA or kArSyam, pari-;(2) kzIRatA, etc.

LEANNESS , s. kfSatA -tvaM, kArSyaM, parikfSatA, kfSANgatA, kzAmatA, SarIra- kzIRatA, mAMsakzIRatA, kzIRatA, amAMsatvaM, apuzwatA, vipuzwatA, tanutA -tvaM, tAnavaM SarIraSozaRaM, mAMsaSuzkatA, SuzkANgatA.

Leap, v. i. plu 1 A, ut-plu, valg 1 P; nft 4 P; ‘l(eap) down’ avatF 1 P, avaplu; ‘l(eap) up’ utpat, utplu; ‘l(eap) over’ laMG 1 A, 10, atikram 1 U, 4 P, ati-i 2 P. s. pluti f., plutaM, plavaH, valgitaM, JaMpaH, plavanaM; ‘quick (deerʼs) l(eap)’ hariRaplutaM; ‘going by l(eap)s’ plutagati, plavaga. [Leap]ing, s. plavanaM, valgitaM, plutiH, ‘l(eaping) over a period’ maMqUkaplutiH.
LEAP (subs.): (1) plutiH or plu tam, deer's l.: hariRaplu tam, U. ;(2) lamPaH or BampaH (mpA) (= jumping), and those l. s to hell pAtAlaBampASca tAH, Vi. v. 53.; (3) valgitam (= skipping).

LEAP (v.): (1) plavate (plu, c. 1.): l. down: ava- plavate; l. up: utplavate; l. forth: Aplavate;(2) valgate, -ti (valg, c. 1.) (= to skip);(3) lamPaM or BampaM dadAti. L. over: (lamPena, etc.) laNGayati (laNG, c. 10.).

To LEAP , v. n. plu (c. 1. plavate, plotuM), valg (c. 1. valgati -lgituM), Avalg, nft (c. 4. nftyati, narttituM), JampaM kf, utPAlaM kf, visPul (c. 6. -sPulati -lituM); ‘to leap up,’ utplu, samutplu, utpat (c. 1. -patati -tituM), protpat; ‘to leap down,’ avaplu; ‘to leap over,’ laNG (c. 10. laNGayati -yituM), vilaNG, ullaNG, aBilaNG; ‘to leap forth from,’ praskand (c. 1. -skandati -skantuM), protpat.
LEAP , s. plavaH -vanaM, plutaM, valgitaM, JampaH -mpA -laNGanaM, utplavanaM, utplutaM avaskandaH, utPAlaH; ‘going by leaps,’ plutagatiH -tiH -ti, plavagaH -gA -gaM
LEAP-FROG: darduraplAvaH, B.p. x. 18. 15.; maRqUka- plu tiH, com.
LEAP-YEAR: *aDivarzaH (after aDimAsaH): v. Bissextile.
LEAP-YEAR , s. caturTaH saMvatsaro yasminn aDikadivaso niveSyate, aDikadi- navatsaraH, aDikadivasavarzaH.
LEAPED , p. p. plutaH -tA -taM, valgitaH -tA -taM, laNGitaH -tA -taM.
LEAPER , s. plavakaH, plavaH, plavanakArI m. (n), JampI m. (n), valgitakft.
LEAPING (subs.): plutiH; plavanam: v. Leap.
LEAPING , part. plavamAnaH -nA -naM, plavaH -vA -vaM, valgan -lgantI -lgat (t); ‘leaping up,’ utpatizRuH -zRuH -zRu, utplutya.
LEAPING , s. (The act) plavanam, plutakaraRaM, JampakaraRaM; ‘leaping up,’ utplavanaM, utpatanaM; ‘leaping down,’ avaskandaH; ‘leaping over,’ laNGanaM, ullaNGanaM.
LEAPINGLY: i. e. by leaps: plu tEH, U.; etc.

Learn, v. i. Sikz 1 A, aDi-i 2 A, paW 1 P, aDigam 1 P, aByas 4 U; aByAsena vidyAM laB 1 A or prAp 5 P. v. i. jYA 1 U, avagam, vid 2 P, buD 1 P, upalaB, Sru 5 P, gfhItArTa a. BU 1 P; See Know. [Learn]ed, a. vidvas (duzI f.), vipaScit, jYA-nin, vidyA-viSizwa-saMpanna-vat, kfta-upAtta-vidya paMqita, buDa, prA(pra)jYa; jYAnavat, vyutpanna, bahuSruta, sUri, vidyAvfdDa, sAkzara. 2 aDItin, vicakzaRa, vijYa, kuSala, nipuRa, pravIRa, catura; kovida, jYa, vid in comp. 3 (Of books &c.) pAMqityasya sUcaka, jYAnasya gamaka; ‘a l(earned) man’ paMqitaH, vipaScit, sUriH, buDaH, &c.; ‘l(earned) in law’ smftijYa, nyAyavid [Learn]edly, adv. paMqitavat, prajYavat, sajYAnaM, nipuRatayA, sakOSalaM. [Learn]er, s. SizyaH, CAtraH, aDyetf m., vidyArTin m. [Learn]ing, s. vidyA, vidvattA, vidvattvaM, jYAnaM, pAMqityaM, vyutpatti f., prAjYatA, vidyAsaMpad f. 2 (Act) aDyayanaM, SikzaRaM, aByAsaH, vidyArjanaM, vidyAprApti f., jYAnAgamaH. 3 SAstraM, vidyA; ‘sacred l(earning)’ Sruti f., nigamajYAnaM; ‘he affects great l(earning)’ paMqitaMmanyaH, paMqitAyate (D.).

LEARN: I To gain knowledge:(1) Sikzate (Sikz, c. 1.), shall not l. the language of barbarians: na mlecCaBAzAM Sikzeta, Vas.;(2) aDyeti (i, c. 2 (gen. = to study), he l. t the Vedas as well as their limbs in their entirety: aDyagIzwa sa vedAMSca vedANgAni ca savarSaH, Mah. i. 128. 37.;(3) SikzAM gfhRAti (grah, c. 9 (with gen.), V. p.II To get information: avagacCati (gam, c. 1.): v. To know, understand.III To teach: q. v.

To LEARN , v. a. (Acquire knowledge of any thing by study, &c.) Sikz (c. 1. Sikzate -kzituM), upaSikz, aDI (c. 2. aDIte, aDyetuM, rt. i), aDigam (c. 1. -gacCati -gantuM), paW (c. 1. paWati -WituM), aByas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM), aDyayanena or aByAsena vidyAM grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or laB (c. 1. laBate, labDuM) or prAp (c. 5. -Apnoti -AptuM) or avAp, aByAsaM kf, vidyAByAsaM kf, vidyAgamaM kf. — (Gain the knowledge of, become informed of) jYA (c. 9. jAnAti -nIte jYAtuM), parijYA, avagam, upalaB, vijYaptaH -ptA -ptaM BU, gfhItArTaH -rTA -rTaM BU; ‘to learn by heart,’ aByas.
To LEARN , v. n. SikzAM kf, aDyayanaM kf, aDigamaM kf, aByAsaM kf, vidyA- ByAsaM kf, vidyAprAptiM kf, vidyAgrahaRaM kf, vidyAlabDiM kf, vidyAgamaM kf.

LEARNED: I Erudite:(1) vidvas (f. -duzI); [Page412] (2) paRqitaH (tA, taM);(3) vipaScit (mfn.); (4) buDaH (DA, DaM), vi-.II L. in:(1) aBijYaH (jYA, jYaM): v. Knowing;(2) aDItin (f. nI), l. in the four Vedas: aDItI caturzvAmnAyezu, D. v.: v. Proficient.III Of works etc.: pARqitya- vyaYjaka (f. YjikA) (= indicative of learing) (?).

LEARNED , LEARNT, p. p. SikzitaH -tA -taM, aDItaH -tA -taM, aDigataH -tA -taM, aByastaH -stA -staM, paWitaH -tA -taM, avagataH -tA -taM, upalabDaH -bDA -bDaM; ‘learnt by heart,’ aByastaH -stA -staM, kaRWasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘to be learnt,’ SikzitavyaH -vyA -vyaM, aByasyaH -syA -syaM, aByasanIyaH -yA -yaM.

LEARNED , a. (Versed in literature and science) vidvAn -duzI -dvat (s), paRqitaH -tA -taM, jYAnI -ninI -ni (n), vidyAvAn -vatI -vat (t), vidyAviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, vidyAsampannaH -nnA -nnaM, kftavidyaH -dyA -dyaM, vidyAlaNkftaH -tA -taM, savidyaH -dyA -dyaM, labDavidyaH &c., vEdyaH -dyI -dyaM, jYAnavAn &c., vipaScit m. f. n., prAjYaH -jYA -jYaM, prajYaH -jYA -jYaM, prajYAvAn &c., vyutpannaH -nnA -nnaM, kftaDIH -DIH -Di, aDIyAnaH -nA -naM, aDItI -tinI &c., bahuSrutaH -tA -taM, kovidaH -dA -daM, manIzI -ziRI -zi (n), budDimAn &c., DImAn &c., buDaH -DA -DaM, DIraH -rA -raM, saMKyAvAn &c., kaviH -viH -vI -vi, sUriH &c., sUrI -riRI -ri (n), kftI -tinI -ti (n), labDavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, akzarasampannaH -nnA -nnaM, sAkzaraH -rA -raM, sArasvataH -tI -taM, aDyayanasampannaH &c., vidyAvfdDaH -dDA -dDaM, san satI sat, tattvadarSI -rSinI -rSi (n), dIrGadarSI &c., dUradarSI &c.; ‘a learned man,’ vidvajjanaH, paRqitaH, buDaH, sarvvarasaH; ‘learned in the Vedas,’ SrotriyaH, vedavid, vedavidvAn m. (s), anucAnaH, CAndasaH. — (Conversant with, skilled in) aBijYaH -jYA -jYaM, vijYaH -jYA -jYaM, viSAradaH -dA -daM, vicakzaRaH -RA -RaM, nipuRaH -RA -RaM, kuSalaH -lA -laM, pravIRaH -RA -RaM, caturaH -rA -raM, vettA -ttrI -ttf (ttf), jYaH jYA jYaM or vid in comp.; as, ‘learned in the law,’ smftijYaH &c., Darmmavid m. f. n., ‘learned in music,’ gAnDarvvatattvajYaH.
LEARNEDLY: (1) pARqityena (?);(2) vEduzyeRa (?).
LEARNEDLY , adv. paRqitavat, sapARqityaM, pARqityena, prAjYavat, vidvajjanavat, savidyaM, vEduzyeRa, sajYAnaM, jYAnapUrvvaM.
LEARNER: (1) SikzA- or vidyA-grAhaka (f. hikA); (2) SizyaH (= pupil).
LEARNER , s. SizyaH, vidyArTI m. (n), aDyetA m. (tf), aDyAyI m. (n), SikzitAkzaraH, vidyAByAsakarttA m. (rttf), aByAsakft.

LEARNING (subs.): (1) vidyA, as a rule, men of equal l. cavil at eacteach other's reputation: prAyaH samAnavidyAH parasparayaSaHpuroBAgAH, Mal i. 19.;(2) SikzA, (rare), they may show their l.: te darSayeyuH svAM SikzAm, Mah. i. 132. 3.;(3) pARqityam (= erudition);(4) vEduzyam (= 3.: rare); (5) aBijYatA (= knowingness): v. Proficient.

LEARNING , s. (Knowledge of literature, erudition) vidyA, pARqityaM, jYAnaM, vijYAnaM, vEduzyaM, vidvattA, jYAtftvaM, vyutpattiH f., prAjYatvaM, paRqitatA -tvaM, vettftvaM, vidyAsampattiH f., akzarasampattiH f., sAkzaratA, aDyayanasampattiH f. — (Literature) vidyA, SAstraM, akzaraM, sAhityaM. — (Sacred learning) SrutiH f., SrotriyatvaM. — (Act of learning, acquisition of learning) SikzA, aDyayanaM, aByAsaH, vidyAByAsaH, vidyAprAptiH f., vidyAlabDiH f., vidyArjanaM, vidyAgamaH; ‘cultivation of learning,’ vidyAnusevanaM; ‘patronising learning,’ vidyAnu- pAlanaM; ‘to affect great learning,’ paRqita (nom. paRqitAyate).

sanskrit.iast: vihitakālaṃ yāvad niyamitamūlyam apekṣya kṣetragṛhādīnāṃ parahastasamarpaṇaṃ

sanskrit.iast: paṭṭolikāpūrvvaṃ niyamitamūlyam apekṣya kṣetragṛhādi paraprayojanīyaṃ dā

details.body: Lease, s. pawwaH, pawwolikA. v. t. Avihita kAlAt nirUpitamUlyena dA 3 U or visfj 6 P.
LEASE (subs.): pawwaH or pawwolikA (?).
LEASE (v.): pawwena dadAti (?) (after Bengali): v. Also to hire.
LEASE , s. (Of lands, houses, &c.) pawwaH, pawwolikA, kxptakIlA, vihitakAlaM yAvad niyamitamUlyam apekzya kzetragfhAdInAM parahastasamarpaRaM.

To LEASE , v. a. pawwaM dA, pawwolikAM dA, pawwena kzetragfhAdi paraprayojanIyaM dA, pawwolikApUrvvaM niyamitamUlyam apekzya kzetragfhAdi paraprayojanIyaM dA or visfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), AvihitakAlAd nirUpitamUlyam apekzya kzetragfhAdi parahaste samf in caus. (-arpayati -yituM).
LEASED , p. p. pawwena or pawwaliKanapUrvvam AvihitakAlAt parahastasamarpitaH -tA -taM.
LEASEHOLD: pawwakftaH (tA, taM) (?).
LEASEHOLD , a. pawwena or pawwolikAliKanapUrvvam aDyuzitaH -tA -taM.
Leash, s. carmabaMDaH, carmarajju f. 2 trayaM, tritayaM.
LEASH: I A thong: carmabanDaH.II Three: trayam.
LEASH , s. (Leather thong) carmmabanDaH -nDanI, carmmarajjuH m. f., banDa- narajjuH. — (Tierce, three) trayaM, trikaM; ‘a leash of hares,’ SaSakatrayaM.
To LEASH , v. a. carmmarajjunA or carmmarajvA banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM).
LEASING , s. asatyatA, anftatA, alIkatA, kApawyaM, mfpAvAdaH. See FALSEHOOD.

Least, a. aRu, alpa, stoka, atyalpa, alpizWa, kanizWa, stokatama, alpatama, kzodizWa; ‘the l(east) sorrow’ aRurapi SokaH ‘the l(east) particle’ lavaH, leSaH, aRuH, kaRaH. adv. stokaM, alpizWaM, kiMcit, kiyat; ‘in the l(east)’ manAgapi, alpamapi, stokAMSenApi, stokamapi, leSamapi, kimapi, kiMcidapi; ‘at l(east)’ ex. by avara a. in comp.; ‘witnesses should be at l(east) three’ tryavarAH sAkziRo jYeyAH (Y. ii. 69); ‘at l(east) 100 Rs.’ SatAvarA rUpakAH; oft. by tAvat, ‘at l(east) once’ sakfdapi tAvat.
LEAST (adj.): expr. by words given under little with api, (you) should not feel the l. sorrow for it: alpo'pi nAtra kartavyaH SokaH, V. p.; the l. acceptance: aRurapi parigrahaH, K.
LEAST (adv.): (1) atyalpam;(2) alpizWam, etc.
LEAST, AT: antataH, Kav.: v. Also certainly.
LEAST, THE or IN THE (adv.): (1) alpamapi; (2) aRvapi;(3) manAgapi; etc.

LEAST , a. (Smallest) alpizWaH -zWA -zWaM, kanizWaH -zWA -zWaM, kzudratamaH -mA -maM, kzodizWaH -zWA -zWaM, kanIyAn -yasI -yaH (s), tanizWaH -zWA -zWaM, tanI- yAn &c., laGizWaH &c., stokatamaH -mA -maM, sUkzmatamaH -mA -maM, atikzudraH -drA -draM, svalpaH -lpA -lpaM, avaraH -rA -raM, avaratamaH -mA -maM, nyUnaH -nA -naM; ‘least of all,’ sarvvakanizWaH -zWA -zWaM, sarvvakanIyAn &c., sarvvasmAt kzudraH -drA -draM; ‘the least particle,’ leSaH, lavaH, kaRaH; ‘not the least darkness is in that place,’ tatra anDakArasya leSo'pi nAsti.

LEAST , adv. (In the least) manAk, kiYcit, alpizWaM, kanizWaM, leSamapi, kiyat, sfkzmaM, stokaM; ‘not in the least,’ na manAk, na manAgapi, na kiYcidapi, na kimapi, na kiyadapi, na sUkzmamapi, na stokamapi, na leSamapi, aleSaM; ‘three witnesses at least,’ tryavarAH sAkziRaH; ‘at least, at any rate,’ tAvat.

Leather, s. parizkftaM carma; ‘l(eather) bag’ carmaBa-strikA, carmaprasevikA; ‘l(eather)-bottle’ kutU f., ‘a small l(eather)-bottle’ kutupaH, ‘l(eather)-dresser’ carmakft, carmakAraH; ‘l(eather)-seller’ carmavikra-yin. Leathern, a. carmakfta-nirmita, carma-maya (yI f.), carma in comp.
LEATHER: carman (n.), l. bag: carmaBastrikA, D.

LEATHER , s. carmma n. (n), dftiH m., paSutvak f. (c), paSucarmma n., kfttiH f., ajinaM, vardDaM, SipiH f.; ‘a leather thong,’ carmmabanDaH -nDanaM, varatrA, vardDrI; ‘covered with leather,’ carmmAvftaH -tA -taM, carmmAvanadDaH -dDA -dDaM, carmmAcCAditaH -tA -taM.
LEATHER , a. carmma in comp., carmmamayaH -yI -yaM; ‘a leather shoe,’ carmmapAdukA; ‘a leather band,’ carmmabanDaH. See LEATHERN.
To LEATHER , v. a. carmmadaRqena taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM) or prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM).
LEATHER-BOTTLE: dftiH (rare).
LEATHER-CUTTER , s. carmmaCid m., carmmaCedanakArA m. (n), carmmAvakarttI m.
LEATHER-DRESSER: *carmasaMskArakaH.
LEATHER-DRESSER , s. carmmakAraH -rakaH, carmmakArI m. (n), carmmakft, carmmAraH.
LEATHER-SELLER , s. carmmavikretA m. (tf), carmmavikrayI m. (n), carmmavi- krayopajIvI m.
LEATHERN: (1) carma- in comp.;(2) carmamayaH (yI, yaM);(3) cArmikaH (kI, kaM) (rare).

LEATHERN , a. cArmmikaH -kI -kaM, cArmmaH -rmmI -rmmaM, carmmI -rmmiRI -rmmi (n), carmmamayaH -yI -yaM, carmmanirmmitaH -tA -taM, dArtteyaH -yI -yaM, aji- nIyaH -yA -yaM, paSutvaNmayaH -yI -yaM, carmma in comp.; ‘a leathern bottle,’ dftiH m.
LEATHERY: carmasadfSaH (SI, SaM); better with adv. carmavat.
LEATHERY , a. carmmavad duHKaBedyaH -dyA -dyaM, carmmasaguRaH -RA -RaM.

Leave, s. anujYA-jYAnaM, anumati f., anumodanaM. 2 AmaMtraRaM, ApracCanaM; ‘to take or ask l(eave) of’ AmaMtr 10 A, ApracC 6 A; See Adieu; ‘to give l(eave)’ anujYA 9 U, anu-man 4 A, anumud 1 A. v. t. tyaj 1 P, hA 3 P, utsfj 6 P, ujJ 6 P, rah 1 P 10, parihf 1 P, varj 10, nir-, muc 6 P. 2 nirgam 1 P, apagam, apa-i-yA 2 P, apasf 1 P, apakram 1 U, 4 P, (all with abl.). 3 mftyupatreRa dA 3 U; ‘estate left (after death)’ rikTaM. 4 viram 1 P, nivft 1 A (with abl.); muc, tyaj, apAs 4 P; oft. ex. by sTA 1 P, As 2 A; ‘l(eave) it now’ tizWatu-AstAM tadaDunA. 5 nikzip 6 P, nyas, sam-f c. (arpayati); ‘l(eave) everything to him’ sarvaM tadaDInaM kuru. 6 Siz 7 P or c., ava-pari°; ud-vft c., ‘nothing was left’ na kimapyavaSizwaM; ‘to be left’ Siz pass.; ‘we being left behind’ asmAsvavahInezu (S. 2). v. i. nirgam, apa-yA, viram, &c. [Leave] for, prasTA 1 A (with acc.). [Leave] off, viram, nivft, tyaj; See above. ‘the peacock left off daneing’ parityaktanartano mayUraH (S. 6). ‘when it left off raining’ SAMte pAnIyavarze (H. 3). [Leave] out, vfj, parityaj. Leavings, s. SezaH-zaM, paMri-ava°; SizwaM, ava-pari°, SezaBAgaH-KaMqaH, udvartaH, ucCizwaM. 2 malaM; ‘l(eavings) of food’ SezAnnaM, Bakzita-Bukta-SezaH-zaM, BuktAvaSizwaM, ucCizwaM, BuktojJitaM; ‘one who eats l(eaving)’ SezaBojin, ucCizwASanaH.

LEAVE (subs.): I Permission: q. v.: anujYA. Ph.: by your l.: tavAnumate, Mah.II Depar- -ture: vidAyaH, give me l. (to depart): vidAyo dIyatAmiti, Ma. n. v. 99. L. (of absence): vidAyaH (used in Bengali); privilege l.: *deyavidAyaH.

To LEND , v. a. (Give to another for temporary use) nirUpitakAlaM yAvat kiYcid dravyaM paraprayojanIyaM dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM), Avihita- kAlAt prayojyaM kiYcid dravyaM parahaste samf in caus. (-arpayati -yituM) or f or nikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM) or nyas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM) or parasmin samf, nirUpitakAle pratidAtavyaM or pratideyaM kiYcid dravyaM dA or samf, nirUpitakAlaparyyantaM dravyaprayogaM kf. — (Give to be returned in kind, as money, a loaf of bread, &c.) fRaM dA, [Page447-b+ 51] fRa samf or f in caus., fRadAnaM kf; ‘to lend money,’ DanaprayogaM dA or kf, paraprayojyaM DanaM dA, AvihitakAlAt prayojanIyaM DanaM parasmE dA or parasmin samf; ‘to lend money at interest,’ kusIdaM kf, kOsIdyaM kf, kalAmbikAM kf; ‘lend me three loaves of bread,’ pUpatrayaM mahyaM fRaM dehi. — (Grant, furnish, afford) dA, pradA, f, samf, parikxp (c. 10. -kalpayati -yituM), upasTA in caus. (-sTApayati -yituM); ‘he lends an ear,’ karRaM dadAti, karRam arpayati, karRArpaRaM karoti; ‘to lend assistance,’ upakf, sAhAyyaM kf.

Samaka, SAMtida, SAMtikara (rI f.). 2 snigDa, cikkaRa. s. pra-upa-SamanaM, kleSApahaM, SUlaGnaM.
LENIENT: (1) sadayaH (yA, yaM): v. Kind, merci- -ful;(2) mfdu (f. dvI): v. Mild.

LENIENT , a. kzamAvAn -vatI -vat (t), kzamI -miRI -mi (n), mfduH -du -dvI -du, sOmyaH -myA -myaM, snigDaH -gDA -gDaM, komalaH -lA -laM, anugraH -grA -graM, sAmabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, atIkzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, atIvraH -vrA -vraM, aparuzaH -zA -zaM, anugradaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, sadayaH -yA -yaM, dayArdraH -rdrA -rdraM, dayAluH -luH -lu, sAmopacArI -riRI -ri (n), kfpAluH -luH -lu. — [Page448-a+ 51] (Assuasive) SamakaH -kA -kaM, SamI -minI -mi (n). See LENITIVE; ‘a lenient measure,’ sAmopacAraH, sAmopAyaH.
LENIENTLY: (1) sadayam (= kindly);(2) mfdu (= mildly).
LENIENTLY , adv. kzamApUrvvaM, kzamayA, anugraM, atIkzRaM, sAmnA, samArdavaM, sadayaM, dayayA, snigDaM, aparuzaM, komalaM.
To LENIFY , v. a. Sam (c. 10. Samayati -yituM), upaSam, praSam, sAntv or SAntv (c. 10. sAntvayati -yituM), pariSAntv.
LENITIVE , a. SamakaH -kA -kaM, SAntikaH -kI -kaM, SAntikaraH -rA -raM, SAntidaH -dA -daM, SAntikarttA -rttI -rttf (rttf), snehI -hinI -hi (n), snigDaH -gDA -gDaM, snigDakArI &c., cikkaRaH -RA -RaM.
LENITIVE , s. (A medicine that softens pain) vedanASAntikaM, vedanA- Samakam OzaDaM, kleSApahaM, upaSamanaM, praSananaM, SUlaGnaM, sAmopacAraH.
LENITY , s. kzamA, kzamASIlatA, mfdutA, sOmyatA, sAmopacArabudDiH f., anugratA. — (Mildness of discipline) anugradaRqatvaM, atIkzRadaRqatvaM, alpadaRqaH -RqanaM, alpaSikzA. See LENIENCY.
Lens, s. kAcaH; ‘convex l(ens)’ maDyonnatakAcaH; ‘concave l(ens)’ maDyanimnakAcaH; ‘a double convex l(ens)’ yavaH; ‘a crystal l(ens)’ sUryakAMtaH, arkASman m., dIptopalaH.
LENS: *dfzwikAcaH; vIkzaRakAcaH.
LENS , s. kAcaH; ‘a convex lens,’ maDyonnatakAcaH; ‘a double convex lens,’ yavaH; ‘a concave lens,’ maDyanimnakAcaH; ‘a chrystalcrystal lens,’ dIptopalaH, arkASmA m. (n), sUryyASmA m., sUryyakAntaH.
LENT: kuzwIyaparvaBedaH.

LENT , p. p. (Given to another for temporary use) AvihitakA- lAt parahaste samarpitaH -tA -taM or arpitaH -tA -taM or nikziptaH -ptA -ptaM or nyastaH -stA -staM, nirUpitakAlaM yAvad visfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, kAlakftaH -tA -taM, prayuktaH -ktA -ktaM.
LENT , s. (Fast of forty days) catvAriMSaddinaparyyanto mahopavAsaH.
LENTEN: I Lit.: *leRwIyaH (yA, yaM).II Fig.: v. Spare, plain.
LENTEN , a. pUrvvoktamahopavAsasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
Lenticular, a. masUropama.
LENTICULAR , a. masUrasarUpaH -pA -paM, masUropamaH -mA -yaM.
Lentiform, a. yavAkfti, yavarUpa.
LENTIFORM , a. yavasarUpaH -pA -paM, yavAkftiH -tiH -ti, yavAkAraH -rA -raM.
LENTIGINOUS , a. jawulI -linI -li (n), dadruRaH -RA -RaM.
Lentigo, s. jawu(qu)laH, kAlakaH, pipluH. Lentiginous, a. jawulin, kAlakayukta.
LENTIGO , s. (Freckly eruption) jawulotpattiH f., tilakotpattiH f., dadruH m.
Lentil, s. masu(sU)raH-rA.
LENTIL: masUraH or masuraH.
LENTIL , s. masUraH, masuraH, maNgalyakaH.
LENTOR , s. (Viscousness) sAndratA, SyAnatA. — (Slowness) mandatA.
Lentous, a. sAMdra, SyAna, Gana. Lentor, s. sAMdratA, SyAnatA.
LENTOUS , a. sAndraH -ndrA -ndraM, SyAnaH -nA -naM, GanaH -nA -naM.
Leo, s. siMhaH, siMharASiH. Leonine, a. sEMha (hI f.), siMhaSIla-Darman.
LEO , s. (The sign of the zodiac) siMhaH, AraRyarASiH m.
LEONINE: sEhaH (hI, haM). Ph.: l. verse: *lEyanacCandaH.
LEONINE , a. sEMhaH -hI -haM, sEMhikaH -kI -kaM, siMhaDarmmA -rmmA -rmma (n), siMhasvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, siMhaSIlaH -lA -laM, siMhasambanDI -nDinI &c.
Leopard, s. citrakaH, citravyAGraH.
LEOPARD: (1) citrakaH;(2) upavyAGraH.
LEOPARD , s. citrakaH, citravyAGraH, tarakzuH -kzukaH, SvavyAGraH, pfdAkuH m., puRqarIkaH, mfgAdanaH.

Leper, s. kuzWin m., Svitrin m., kuzWarogin m., kuzWapIqitaH. Leprosy, s. kuzWaM, SvitraM, koWaH, maMqalakaM, kuzWarogaH, tvagrogaH, duScarman n., ‘black l(eprosy)’ mahArogaH, mahAvyADiH, rakta-kuzWaM; ‘wasting l(eprosy)’ galatkuzWaM. Leprous, a. kuzWin, Svitrin, kuzWapIqita.
LEPER: (1) kuzWin (f. nI), M.;(2) kuzWarogin (f. RI);(3) kuzWapIqitaH (tA, taM), Sr.
LEPER , s. kuzWI m. -zWinI f., SvitrI m. -triRI f. (n), tvagrogI m. -giRI f. (n), kuzWarogI &c., duzwacarmmA m. (n), duScarmmA m.
LEPORINE , a. SaSasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), SaSakIyaH -yA -yaM.
LEPROSY: (1) kuzWam;(2) mahAvyADiH (a gen. term). Spotted l.: citram.

LEPROSY , s. kuzWaM, kuzWarogaH, SvitraM, SvEtraM, SvetaM, SvEtyaM, tvagrogaH, tvagdozaH, carmmadUzikA, duzwacarmmatvaM, duScarmmatvaM, siDmalA, citraM, maRqalakaM, koWaH; ‘black leprosy,’ raktakuzWaM, mahArogaH, mahAvyADiH m., vyADiH; ‘afflicted with it,’ raktakuzWI m. (n), mahArogI m. (n); ‘white leprosy,’ SvetakuzWaM; ‘wasting leprosy,’ galatkuzWaM.
LEPROUS: (1) kuzWin (f. nI);(2) kuzWarogAkrAntaH (ntA, ntaM).

LEPROUS , a. kuzWI -zWinI -zWi (n), SvitrI -triRI -tri (n), kuzWarogI -giRI -gi (n), tvagrogI &c., carmmarogI &c., duzwacarmmA -rmmA -rmma (n), duScarmmA &c., mahArogI &c., mahAvyADigrastaH -stA -staM.
Lesion, s. apakAraH, pIqA, kzati f.
LESION , s. kzatiH f., parikzatiH f. -taM, apakAraH, drohaH, pIqA, bADaH.

Less, a. nyUna, Una, alpatara, alpIyas, kzudratara, stokatara, sUkzmatara. adv. nyUnaM, alpaM, &c.; ‘no l(ess) than’ ex. by avara a.; tryavarAH sA-kziRaH; ‘much l(ess)’ kimuta, kiM punaH, kimu; ‘a little l(ess) than 10,000 years’ kiMcidUnaM SaradAmayutaM (R. x. 1); (as a suffix) ex. by a, nir, vihIna, rahita, varjita, vIta, vigata, in comp. [Less]en, v. t. nyUnIkf 8 U, Un 10, hras c., apa-ci 5 U, laGUkf, laGayati (D.), kzi 1, 5 P or c. v. i. hras 1 P, nyUnIBU 1 P, alpIBU, kzi-apaci- pass. [Less]er, a. kzudratara, &c.
LESS (adj.): (1) nyUnaH (nA, naM);(2) UnaH (nA, naM), if it is l.: UnAYcet, V. s.: v. Little.
LESS (adv.): (1) nyUnam;(2) alpataram (?). Much l.: q. v.: kimuta.
LESS (suff.): (1) a- (or an- before vowels), childless: aputraH (trA, traM) or anapatyaH (tyA, tyaM); (2) nir-, fearless: nirBayaH (yA, yaM): v. Devoid of.

LESS , a. nyUnaH -nA -naM, UnaH -nA -naM, alpataraH -rA -raM, alpIyAn -yasI -yaH (s), alpaH -lpA -lpaM, kzudrataraH -rA -raM, kzodIyAn &c., kanIyAn &c., stokataraH -rA -raM, tanIyAn &c., mUkzmataraH -rA -raM, avaraH -rA -raM with abl. c.; as, ‘water is less heavy than quicksilver,’ [Page448-b+ 51] jalagurutvaM pAradagurutvAd alpaM Bavati; ‘less or more,’ nyUnADikaM, nyUnAtirekaM. The privative affix ‘less’ is expressed by hInaH -nA -naM, rahitaH -tA -taM, virahitaH &c., vihInaH &c., SUnyaH &c., varjjitaH &c., apetaH &c., vyatiriktaH &c. affixed, or by a, nir, ni, vi, vIta, vigata prefixed; as, ‘childless,’ putrahInaH -nA -naM, aputraH -trA -traM, nizputraH &c.; ‘penniless,’ dravyahInaH &c., nizkiYcanaH &c.; ‘senseless,’ budDihInaH &c., nirbudDiH &c.; ‘worthless,’ sArahInaH &c., nirguRaH &c.; ‘fearless,’ vItaBayaH &c., aBayaH &c.
LESS , adv. nyUnaM, alpataraM, alpaM, kzudrataraM, stokaM, stokataraM with abl. c. See LESS, a. ‘How much less,’ kimuta, kimpunar.
LESS , s. nyUnatvaM, UnatA, alpatvaM -tA. — (An inferior) avarajanaH.
Lessee, s. pawwolikADArin m.
LESSEE: BAwakena kzetrAdigrahItf (m.).
LESSEE , s. pawwaDArI m. (n), pawwolikADArI m., pawwagrAhI m., pawwAdAyI m.
LESSEN: nyUnIkaroti (trans) or nyUnIBavati (in- -trans): v. To diminish.
To LESSEN , v. a. nyUnIkf, alpIkf, Un (c. 10. Unayati -yituM), nyUn, hras (c. 10. hrAsayati -yituM), kan (c. 10. kanayati -yituM), laGa (nom. laGayati -yituM), laGUkf.
To LESSEN , v. n. nyUnIBU, UnIBU, alpIBU, hras (c. 1. hrasate -situM), kzi in pass. (kzIyate), apaci in pass. (-cIyate); ‘to lessen by a quarter,’ pAdaSo nyUnIBU.
LESSENED , p. p. nyUnIBUtaH -tA -taM, alpIBUtaH -tA -taM, hrasitaH -tA -taM.
LESSER , a. alpaH -lpA -lpaM, alpataraH -rA -raM, alpIyAn -yasI -yaH (s), kzudrataraH -rA -raM, kzudraH -drA -draM, avaraH -rA -raM.
Lesson, s. pAWaH, aDyAyaH. 2 SAsanaM, upadeSaH, boDaH-DanaM, SikzA. 3 vAgdaMqaH, BartsanaM; ‘take l(esson) from’ upadeSaM grah 9 U. v. t. upadiS 6 P, SAs 2 P.

LESSON: I That which is taught:(1) pAWyam, read boy's l. s: papAWa bAlapAWyAni, V. p.;(2) SikzA (= instruction), to take l.: SikzAM gfhvAti, Mah.II A portion to learn at one time: pAWaH.III Reproof: SAsanam, to give l.: SAsanaM karoti.
LESSON , s. pAWaH -WanaM, aDyAyaH, aDyayaH -yanaM, nipAWaH, vyAKyAnaM. — (Precept, matter inculcated) upadeSaH, SikzA, aDyApanaM, boDanaM, nirdeSaH. — (Reprimand) vAgdaRqaH, vAkSAsanaM.
To LESSON , v. a. upadiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), Sikz (c. 10. Sikzayati -yituM), aDI in caus. (aDyApayati -yituM), SAs (c. 2. SAsti, SAsituM), upadeSaM kf.
LESSOR (v.): pawwadAtf (f. trI) (??).
LESSOR , s. pawwadAtA m. (tf), pawwolikAdAtA m., pawwadAyI m. (n).

sanskrit.iast: pāpaṃ mā kuru pāpe hi kṛte

sanskrit.word: सावधाना भवत कोऽपि युप्मान् न भ्रमयेत्
