sanskrit.iast: tathā prayatethā yathā na pralomyasepralobhyase vanitābhiḥ

details.body: Lest, conj. nocet, anyaTA; ‘love not sleep l(est) thou come to want’ taMdrAsakto mA Bava nocet akiMcano Bavizyasi; sometimes ex. by na iti or kadAcit with pot. or mA with simple future or imperative; mA kasyApi tapasvino haste patizyati (S. 2) ‘l(est) she fall into the hands &c.’ mAsyA vikAro varDatAM (M. 4); ‘l(est) he should kill us’ mA no hiMsIditi; ‘beware l(est) you be enticed by women’ taTA prayateTA yaTA na pralomyasepraloByase vanitABiH (Ka. 109).
LEST: expr. by kadAcit with viDiliN, l. he see you: kadAcit tvAM sa paSyet; nocet with law: v. Otherwise.

LEST , conj. yadi, yadi na, cet, na cet, no cet, yadi kadAcit, yadA- kadAcit, kadAcit. In using these particles to express the word ‘lest’ it will be necessary to vary the form of the sentence according to the particle employed, as in the following examples selected from modern Sanskrit. ‘I fear lest your minds should be corrupted,’ ced yuzmAkaM manAMsi duzyeyur mamEzA BItir jAyate; ‘beware lest he strike thee,’ sAvaDAno Bava cet tvAmapi tAqayati; or the particle may be omitted; as, ‘beware lest any man deceive you,’ sAvaDAnA Bavata ko'pi yupmAn na Bramayet: or other particles may be used in more classical Sanskrit, the construction of the sentence being changed accordingly; as, ‘commit not evil lest thou obtain the same,’ pApaM mA kuru pApe hi kfte tvayA tAdfSaM prAptavyaM; ‘he commanded to kill the captives lest they should escape,’ vandayaH palAyizyante ityASaNkayA or iti budDyA tAn hantum AdideSa; ‘justice is not to be killed, lest being killed, it destroy us,’ Darmmo na hantavyo mA no Darmmo hato baDIt.

Let, v. t. anujYA 9 U, anuman 4 A, anu-mud 1 A, sah 1 A; oft. ex. by the imperative of aorist forms without a; ‘l(et) it not so happen’ evaM mA BUt. 2 BAwakena dA 3 U; mUlyena dA or visfj 6 P, 3 ruD 7 U, nivAr 10; staMB 9 P. 4 (Blood) sru c., mokz 10; See Bleed; ‘l(et) alone’ na upadru 1 P, na bAD 1 A, oft. by As 2 A, sTA 1 P; ‘now l(et) it alone’ AstAM tattaTEva; ‘l(et) go’, ‘l(et) loose’ muc 6 P or c., mokz, SiTilIkf 8 U; SiTilayati (D.), sraMs c., visfj, Sra(SraM)T-SlaT 1 P, 10; ‘l(ett)ing his hand go’ mukta-srasta-SiTilita-hastaH; ‘l(et) slip’ muc, vikzip 6 P, muDA yA c. (yApayati). [Let] down, avatF c., avaruh c. (ropayati), ava-ni-pat c., avamuc, avasfj, aDaH ni-DA 3 U or sTA c. (sTApayati). [Let] in, praviS c.; aByaMtarIkf. [Let] off, nir-vi-muc; prAs, kzip, Ir c., visfj, mokza; ‘l(et) off with a fine’ daMqadAnena vimukta. [Let] out, muc, mokz. 2 BaMj 7 P, Bid 7 P, prakAS c. (as secrets). 3 paRyena dA.

LET: I To allow, permit: q. v.II As sign of imper. mood:(1) by low, let him be entirely so: taTAviDastAvadaSezamastu saH, Ku.; l. him say all he thinks proper to say: ucyatAM sa vacanIyamaSezam, Ki.; l. it be what may be: yadastu tadastu, Ma.;(2) by luN after mA, l. it never come to pass: mA sma BUt, Ki.; l. not cupid enchant you: mA mUmuhadBavantamananyajanmA, Ma.III To lease: BAwakena dadAti, (dA, c. 3.).IV Of blood: srAvayati (c. of sru): v. Bleed.

To LET , v. a. (Permit, allow) anujYA (c. 9. -jAnAti -nIte -jYAtuM), aByanujYA, anuman (c. 4. -manyate -mantuM), sah (c. 1. sahate, soQuM), vizah, anujYAM kf or dA or sometimes expressible by the causal form; as, ‘he lets perish,’ nASayati; ‘he lets enter,’ praveSayati. — (Let out, lease out) vihitakAlaM yAvad nirUpitamUlya- [Page449-a+ 51] mapekzya gfhakzetrAdi paraprayojanIyaM dA or visfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), niyamitamUlyamapekzya kiYcid dravyaM paraprayojanIyaM dA, AvihitakAlAd nirUpitamUlyamapekzya gfhakzetrAdi parahaste samf in caus. (-arpayati -yituM) or f, niyamitapAritozikamapekzya kiYcid vastu parasmin samf. — (Hinder) nivf (c. 10. -vArayati -yituM), ruD (c. 7. ruRadDi, rodDuM), pratiruD, niruD. — (Let alone) tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM), parityaj, visfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM, c. 10. sarjayati -yituM), utsfj. — (Let down) avatF (c. 10. -tArayati -yituM), avaruh in caus. (-ropayati -yituM), avapat (c. 10. -pAtayati -yituM), avamuc (c. 6. -muYcati -moktuM), avasfj. — (Let go, let loose) muc, avamuc, vimuc, visfj, avasfj, SiTi- lIkf, SiTila (nom. SiTilayate -ti -yituM), SlaT (c. 10. SlaTayati -yituM) or SraT, sraMs (c. 10. sraMsayati -yituM), visraMs, visrastaM -stAM kf; ‘having let go the hold,’ srastahastaH -stA -staM, SiTilitahastaH -stA -staM. — (Let in) praviS or niviS or AviS in caus. — (Let out) muc, vimuc, nirmuc, mokz (c. 10. mokzayati -yituM), vimokz, visfj. — (Let off, discharge) muc, pramuc, sfj, as (c. 4. asyati, asituM), prAs, kzip (c. 6. kzipati, kzeptuM), prakzip, Ir (c. 10. Irayati -yituM); ‘let off a gun,’ lohagulikAM yudDanAqeH prakzip or niHsf (c. 10. -sArayati -yituM). See To FIRE. (Let blood) raktaM Sru (c. 10. SrAvayati -yituM). See To BLEED, v. a. (Let slip) muc, vimuc, visfj, SiTilIkf; ‘I will not let slip the occasion,’ avakASaM na SiTilizye. The sense of ‘let’ is often inherent in the imperative; as, ‘let him go,’ gacCatu; ‘let it be,’ Bavatu.
LET ALONE: na bADate (bAD, c. 1.). L. a. its seeing, I have never heard i of it: na ca tAM Sruta- vAnasmi, dUre tadfrSanaM punaH, K. s. xxv. 31. L. a. principle: *nirbADaM tattvam.
LET DOWN: (1) avatArayati (c. of tF);(2) avarohayati (c. of ruh).
LET FLY, LET OFF: muYcati (muc, c. 6.): v. To discharge.
LET Go, LET LOOSE: muYcati or mocayati: v. To release, set free.
LET IN: praveSayati (c. of viS): v. To admit.
LET OUT: I To let go: q. v.II To lease: BAwakena dadAti.
LETHAL: prARaharaH (rA, raM): v. Fatal, deadly.
LETHAL , a. mArAtmakaH -kA -kaM, prARanASakaH -kA -kaM, prARaharaH -rA -raM, prARaGAtakaH -kA -kaM, mftyujanakaH -kA -kaM. See DEADLY.
LETHARGIC, -AL: (1) jaqaH (qA, qaM) (= dull); (2) nidrAlasaH (sA, saM) (= sleepy).

LETHARGIC , a. nidrAluH -luH -lu, atinidrAluH &c., nidrAlasaH -sA -saM, suptabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, jaqaH -qA -qaM, jaqabudDiH &c., nidrASIlaH -lA -laM, svapnaSIlaH -lA -laM, nEdraH -drI -draM, suzupsuH -psuH -psu.
LETHARGICALLY , adv. nidrAluvat, nidrAlasavat, jaqavat, sajAqyaM.

LETHARGICALNESS , LETHARGY, s. nidrAlutA, atinidrAlutvaM, nidrAlasatA, nidrASIlatA, svapnaSIlatA, jaqatA, jAqyaM, jaqabudDitvaM, alasatA, AlasyaM, suptabudDitvaM, SayAlutA, tandrA -ndriH f., pramIlA. — (Deep sleep) Gora- nidrA, gAQanidrA, sunidrA, nirBaranidrA.

Lethargy, s. jAqyaM, maMdatA, nidrAlutA, A-lasya, taMdrA, taMdri-drI f., jaqabudDitvaM, nidrAla-satA, kAryajaqatA, kAryadvezaH, atimAMdyaM. 2 Gora-gAQa-nidrA, nirBaranidrA. [Letharg]ic, a. nidrAlu, nidrAlasa, nidrASIla, jaqa, maMda, jaqabudDi, suptamati; kAryajaqa, kAryavimuKa (KI f.); AlasyaSIla. [Letharg]ically, adv. jaqavat, maMdavat. [Letharg]icalness, See (s.).
LETHARGY: (1) jAqyam (= dullness);(2) nidrAla- satA (= sleepiness);(3) tandrA (= lassitude).
Lethe, s. vismfti f., vismaraRaM, smftinASaH-lopaH. 2 vEtaraRI.
LETHE: vismftiH: v. Forgetfulness.
LETHE , s. vismftiH f., asmftiH f., smftinASaH, smftihAniH f.
LETHEAN , a. vismftijanakaH -kA -kaM, vismftikArakaH -kA -kaM.
LETHIFEROUS , a. mftyujanakaH -kA -kaM, niDanAvahaH -hA -haM. See DEADLY.

Letter, s. akzaraM, varRaH; ‘printing l(etter)’ mudrAkzaraM. 2 leKaH, patraM, leKyaM, saMdeSapatraM; ‘by l(etter)’ patra-dvAreRa; ‘l(etter) from an inferior to a superior’ vijYapti-vijYApanA-patraM; ‘l(etter)-carrier’ patra-vAhaH, leKahAraH. 3 SabdArTaH, akzarArTaH, vAcyArTaH, vacanaM; ‘obey orders to the l(etter)’ yaTAvacanaM AjYAmanuruD 4 A. 4 (Letters) vidyA, jYAnaM; ‘a man of l(etter)s’ kftavidyaH, vidvAn See Learned; ‘l(etter) by l(etter)’ akzaraSaH ‘a dead l(etter)’ luptArTaM vacanaM. v. t. akzarEH aMk 10 or mudra 10. [Letter]ed, a. akzarAMkita, akzaramudrita-cihnita. 2 kftavidya, upAttavidya; See Learned.

LETTER: I Of the alphabet:(1) akzaram;(2) varRaH. The l. a (a), ka (k), etc.: akAraH, kakAraH, etc.; the l. ra (r): rePaH.II Literal statement: SabdArTaH. Ph.: to the l.: yaTAvacanam: v. Also lite- -rally.III An epistle:(1) patram, send a l.: patraM prezaya, A r.;(2) leKaH, to open a l.: leKam unmuYcati, K; to seal a l.: leKaM mudrayati, Mu.; a l. carrier: leKahArakaH, K. Ph.: a man of l.s kftavidya (f. dyA): v. Learned.

LETTER , s. (Of the alphabet, character) akzaraM, varRaH -rRaM, mAtfkA, aBinizWAnaH, arRaH, kAraH; the latter word is only used in naming any letter; as, ‘the letter a,’ akAraH; the letter ‘r,’ is called rePaH. — (Printing letter or type) mudrAkzaraM, akzaramudrA; ‘compound letter,’ saMyuktAkzaraM, sanDyakzaraM; ‘letter by letter,’ akzaraSas; ‘beginning to learn the letters,’ akzarAramBaH. — (Epistle) patraM, leKaH, leKyaM, patrikA, patrI, patrakaM, liKitaM, sandeSapatraM, lipiH f.; ‘by letter,’ patradvArA, patradvAreRa; ‘on sight of the letter,’ patradarSanAt; ‘a letter from an inferior to a superior,’ nivedanapatraM, AvedanapatraM, vijYApanapatraM; ‘from a superior officer,’ AjYApatraM; ‘a letter to a son, daughter, &c.,’ ASI- [Page449-b+ 51] rvAdapatraM. — (The literal meaning, verbal expression) SabdArTaH, akzarArTaH, vAcyArTaH, praTamArTaH, padArTaH, vacanaM, granTArTaH; ‘in the spirit and in the letter,’ arTato granTataSca, arTato vacanataSca. — (Letters, literature) akzaraM, vidyA, SAstraM; ‘a man of letters,’ SikzitAkzaraH, sAkzarajanaH, kftavidyaH. — (Dead letter) nirarTakaviDiH m.

To LETTER , v. a. akzarANkitaM -tAM kf, akzaramudritaM -tAM kf, akzarEr aNk (c. 10. aNkayati -yituM) or mudra (nom. mudrayati -yituM) or mudrIkf or cihna (nom. cihnayati -yituM), akzaracihnitaM -tAM kf, akzarayuktaM -ktAM kf.
LETTER-CARRIER , s. patravAhaH -hakaH, patravAhI m. (n), leKahAraH -rakaH, leKahArI m. (n), leKanikaH.
LETTER-PRESS , s. akzaramudrA, mudrAkzaraM, mudritAkzaraM, akzaraM.
LETTER-WRITER: patraleKakaH and sim. comp.s.
LETTER-WRITER , s. patraleKakaH, patralipikAraH, patraliKanakft.
LETTERED (adj.): i. e. educated, learned: q. v.: kftavidya (f. dyA).

LETTERED , p. p. (Stamped with letters) akzarANkitaH -tA -taM, akzara- mudritaH -tA -taM, akzaracihnitaH -tA -taM, akzarayuktaH -ktA -ktaM; ‘well- lettered,’ SudDavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, SudDAkzaraH -rA -raM. (Versed in lite- rature) SikzitAkzaraH -rA -raM, sAkzaraH -rA -raM, kftavidyaH -dyA -dyaM, gfhI- tavidyaH &c., kftabudDiH -dDiH -dDi.
Lettuce, s. haritakaM, SigruH.
LETTUCE: SAkaBedaH; *laktakam.
LETTUCE , s. SAkaBedaH, haritakaM, SigruH m.
LEUCOPHLEGMACY , s. kaPodaraM, kaPaSoTaH, jalodaraM, udakodaraM, ADmAnaM.
LEUCOPHLEGMATIC , a. kaPodarI -riRI -ri (n), kaPaSoTarogI -giRI -gi (n).
Levant, a. pUrvadeSaja, prAgBava, pOrastya, pUrva-diksTa. s. pUrvadeSaH, prAgdeSaH.
LEVANT: BUmaDyasAgarasya pUrvaprAntaH.
LEVANT , a. pUrvvadeSIyaH -yA -yaM, pUrvvadiSyaH -SyA -SyaM, pUrvvadiksTaH -sTA -sTaM, pUrvvadeSajaH -jA -jaM, pUrvvadeSasambanDI -nDinI &c., sUryyodayadeSasambanDI &c.
LEVANT , s. pUrvvadeSaH, prAgdeSaH, prAcInadeSaH, sUryyodayadeSaH.
Levee, s. rAjadarSanaM, rAjadarSanamelA, darSakamelA.
LEVEE: darSakamelA.
LEVEE , s. rAjadarSanaM, rAjasaBA, saBA, darSanaM, prAtaHsaBA.

Level, a. sama, samasTa, sapAwa, samareKa, samaBU-misTita; ‘lie l(evel) with the ground’ BUmisAtkf pass. 2 kzitijasamasUtra; ‘a l(evel) ground’ samaBUmi f., sAnu m. n., prasTaH, samasTalaM-lI. s. samaM, samaBUmiH-sTalaM, sama-talaM-pfzWaM-deSaH, prasTaH, pradeSasamatA, pAwaH. 2 samatA, tulyatA, sAmyaM, tulya or sama-BAvaH or vftti f.; ‘reduced to the l(evel) of the poor’ daridrasamatAM nIta-gamita; ‘on a l(evel) with’ sama, tulya, samAna; ‘along the l(evel)’ anuprasTaM. 3 lakzyasUtraM-deSaH. 4 niyamaH, sUtraM. v. t. samIkf 8 U; samasTalIkf. 2 lakzyIkf, uddiS 6 P, saM-DA 3 U, prer c. muc 6 P, kzip 6 P. [Level]ler, samakArin m., viSezanASakaH, Beda-BAva-lopakaH. [Level]ness, s. samatA, sAmyaM, samaBUmi-BAvaH.
LEVEL (adj.): samaH (mA, maM), on a l. ground: sama- BUmO; l. with the ground: BUmisamaH (mA, maM).

LEVEL (subs.): I Even surface: samaBUmiH. Ph.: water always finds its own l.: *jalaM sarvatra samaM tizWati.II Equality: q. v.: samatA. Ph.: [Page415] on a l. with: samaH (mA, maM): v. Equal; to rise above the l. of: ativartate (vft, c. 1.).III Ins- -trument for taking l.: sUtram (?), Williams. IV Plan. scheme: q. v.
LEVEL (v.): I To make 1.: samIkaroti, the earth all around was l. ed: kzitiH paritaH samIkftA, Ku. xiv. 44.II To direct: expr. with lakzIkaroti (with acc.).

LEVEL , a. (Even, flat) samaH -mA -maM, samAnaH -nA -naM, samasTaH -sTA -sTaM, sapAwaH -wA -waM, samareKaH -KA -KaM. — (Horizontal) kzitijasamasUtraH -trA -traM. — (On the same plane or line with) samareKaH -KA -KaM, samasUtraH -trA -traM, samadeSasTaH -sTA -sTaM, samaBUmisTaH &c.; ‘level ground,’ samaBUmiH f., samasTalaM -lI, prasTaH, pAwaH, AjiH f.; ‘level surface,’ samapfzWaM, samatalaM.

LEVEL , s. (Even surface) samaM, samasTalaM -lI, samaBUmiH f., samatalaM, samapfzWaM, samadeSaH, prasTaH, pAwaH; ‘liquids always find their own level,’ dravapadArTAH sadA samAnapfzWA Bavanti; ‘the water in the tube rises to a level with the water in the vessel,’ nalasTajalaM prAMSutvena pAtrasTajalasamaM Bavati. — (State of equality, equal eleva- tion) samatA, samAnatA, sAmyaM, tulyatA, samasamAnatA. — (Line of direction in which a weapon is aimed) lakzyaM, lakzyadeSaH, lakzyasUtraM, sanDAnaM, aBisanDAnaM. — (Instrument for finding the level) sUtraM. — (Rule, plan) niyamaH, sUtraM.

To LEVEL , v. a. (Make even) samIkf, samAnIkf, samaM -mAM -maM kf. — (Reduce to an even surface) samasTalIkf, samapfzwIkf, samatalIkf. — (Aim) aBisanDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), pratisanDA, lakzIkf. — (Direct at) uddiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), samuddiS.

LEVELED , p. p. (Made even) samIkftaH -tA -taM, samAnIkftaH -tA -taM. — (Reduced to an even surface) samasTalIkftaH -tA -taM. — (Aimed) pratisaMhitaH -tA -taM, aBisaMhitaH -tA -taM, uddizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
LEVELER , s. samakArI m. (n), samAnakArI m. — (One who destroys distinctions) padanASakaH, padaGAtakaH, BAvaviDAtakaH.
LEVELING , s. samIkaraRaM, samAnIkaraRaM, samasTalIkaraRaM, tulpIkaraRaM.
LEVELLING: I Subs.: samIkaraRam.II Adj.: expr. by part.
LEVELNESS: samatA: v. Equality.
LEVELNESS , s. samatA, sAmyaM, samAnatA -tvaM, samaBUmisTaBAvaH, samasTalasTa- BAvaH, tulyatA.
Lever, s. uttolanadaMqaH; tulAyaMtraM.
LEVER: *tulAyantram.
LEVER , s. uttolanadaRqaH -RqaM, uttolanadAruH m., uttolanI, lohadaRqaH, uttolanayantraM; ‘to raise with a lever,’ lohadaRqena or dAruRA uttul (c. 10. -tolayati -yituM).
LEVERAGE: *tulAyantrayogaH.
Leveret, s. SaSaSiSuH-SAvakaH.
LEVERET: SaSaSAvakaH and sim. comp.s.
LEVERET , s. SaSaSAvakaH, SaSavatsaH, SaSaSiSuH m., bAlaSaSakaH.
LEVIABLE: AdApanIyaH (yA, yaM) (?): v. To levy.
Leviathan, s. timiH, timiMgalaH.
LEVIATHAN: timiNgilaH (?); mAtaNganakraH (?).
LEVIATHAN , s. timiH m., timiNgilaH, mInaraH, samudrAruH m.
Levigate, v. t. cUrR 10, kzud 7 U, piz 7 P. 2 SlakzRIkf 8 U, parizkf.
To LEVIGATE , v. a. (Grind to a fine powder) cUrR (c. 10. cUrRayati -yituM), cUrRIkf. — (Polish, make smooth) parizkf, SlakzRIkf, snigDIkf.
LEVIGATION , s. cUrRIkaraRaM, pezaRaM, kzodIkaraRaM, parizkAraH, SlakzRIkaraRaM.
Levitate, v. t. laGUkf 8 U.
LEVITE: I Lit.: *lEviH.II A priest: puro- hitaH (?).
LEVITE , s. lIvEtAKyo yihudIyAnAM purohitaH or yAjakaH.
Levitical, a. yAjakIya, purohitasaMbaMDin.
LEVITICAL , a. pOrohitaH -tI -taM, yAjakIyaH -yA -yaM, pUrvvoktayAjakasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), DarmmopadeSavizayaH -yA -yaM.
Levity, s. laGutA, lAGavaM, laGiman m., gOrava-hInatA. 2 cApalyaM, cAMcalyaM, taralatA, lo-latA, cApalaM, lOlyaM.
LEVITY: lavutA or lAGavam or laGiman (m.), so that (he) does not understand my l.: na ca me'GigacCati yaTA laGutAm, Si. ix. 56.

LEVITY , s. (Lightness) laGutA, lAGavaM, laGimA m. (n), agurutA. — (Unsteadiness) caYcalatvaM, cAYcalyaM, capalatA, cApalyaM, cApalaM, lolatA, lOlyaM, manolOlyaM, asTiratA, asTEryyaM, anavasTitiH f., aDftiH f. — (Want of seriousness) agurutA, gOravahInatA.

Levy, v. t. (Forces) samA-hf 1 P, SastrAstraM grah c., yudDe vyA-pf c. or pravft c. 2 (A tax) grah 9 U, AdA 3 A, dA c. (dApayati); ‘l(evi)ed taxes from them’ sa tAmyo balimagrahIt (R. i. 18). s. sEnyasamAhAraH. 2 dApanaM, grahaRaM. 3 sEnyasamUhaH.
LEVY (subs.): I Of troops, etc.: utTAnam, sam-. II Of taxes, etc.: samAhAraH.II An army: AsAraH, M. n.
LEVY (v.): I Of troops: utTApayati, sam-, (c. of sTA): v. To raise.II To collect: q. v.: samAharati (hf, c. 1.): v. Also to im- -pose.

To LEVY , v. a. (Raise troops) yodDfmaDye samAropya sEnyAn samUhIkf or vyUhIkf or samUh (c. 1. -Uhate -hituM) or samAhf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), senAM or varUTinIM yuj (c. 10. yojayati -yituM), sEnyasamUhaM kf, sEnyasa- mAhAraM kf, sEnyaparisaMKyAM kf, SastrARi or astrARi grah in caus. (grAhayati -yituM), yudDakarmmaRi pravft (c. 10. -varttayati -yituM), sEnyamaDye aBiliK (c. 6. -liKati -leKituM) or samAruh in caus. (-ropayati -yituM) or Aruh. — (Levy a tax) karaM grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or AdA (c. 3. -dadAti -dAtuM) or dA in caus. (dApayati -yituM) or avahf (c. 10. -hArayati -yituM), SulkagrahaRaM kf. — (Levy contributions) ekEkasmAt kiYcidDanagrahaRaM or DanottolanaM kf.

LEVY , s. (Act of collecting troops) sEnyasamAhAraH, sEnyasamAharaRaM, sEnyABileKanaM, sEnyavyUhakaraRaM. — (Troops raised) sEnyasamUhaH, sEnyasamu- dAyaH. — (Of taxes) karagrahaRaM, SulkagrahaRaM. — (Of money) Danotto- lanaM, ekEkasmAt kiYcidDanagrahaRaM.

Lewd, a. kAmuka, kAmavaSa, suratArTin, laMpawa, BogAsakta, kAmAsakta; See Lustful. 2 duzwa, durAcAra, durvftta, durAtman, pApAtman. [Lewd]ly, adv. kAmukavat, lAMpawyena. [Lewd]ness, s. lAMpawya, BogAsakti f., ratArTitA, vyavAyecCA. 2 duzwatA, durAcAratA, dOrAtmyaM.
LEWD: (1) kAmukaH (kI, kaM);(2) kAmin (f. nI); (3) kAmavaSaH (SA, SaM);(4) kAmarataH (tA, taM).

LEWD , a. kAmukaH -kA -kaM, kAmI -minI -mi (n), ratArTI -rTinI &c., suratArTI &c., vyavAyI -yinI &c., vyavAyaparaH -rA -raM, kAmAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, samBogArTI &c., taralaH -lA -laM, strIlampawaH, lampawaH, strIvyasanI m. — (Wicked) duzwaH -zwA -zwaM, durAcAraH -rA -raM, durAtmA -tmA -tma (n), pApI -pinI -pi (n).
LEWDLY: sakAmaH (mA, maM): v. Lasciviously, lustfully.
LEWDLY , adv. kAmukavat, lampawavat, kAmukaM, sakAmaM, duzwavat.
LEWDNESS: kAmukatA: v. Lust.

LEWDNESS , s. kAmukatvaM, lampawatA, lAmpawyaM, ratArTitvaM, ratAsaktiH f., sakAmatA, samBogArTitvaM, vyavAyaH -yitvaM, vEyAtyaM, viyAtatA, helA, strI- vyasanaM. — (Wickedness) duzwatA, durAcAratA, aDamAcAratA, kusftiH f.
LEXICOGRAPHER: kozakAraH and sim. comp.s.
LEXICOGRAPHER , s. kOSikaH, koSakAraH, koSaracakaH, aBiDAnakarttA m. (rttf).
LEXICOGRAPHICAL , a. kOSikaH -kI -kaM, kozaracanAsambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
LEXICOGRAPHY: kozaracanA (?) and sim. comp.s.
LEXICOGRAPHY , s. SabdakoSaracanA, SabdakoSakaraRaM, kozaracanA.
Lexicon, s. koSaH-zaH; aBiDAnaM, SabdasaMgrahaH-koSaH, niGaMwuH. Lexicographer, s. ko-SakAraH. Lexicography, s. koSaracanA.
LEXICON: kozaH (SaH): v. Dictionary.
LEXICON , s. kozaH, koSaH, SabdakozaH, SabdakoSaH, SabdasaNgrahaH, aBi- DAnaM, SabdagranTaH, SabdajAlaM, nirvacanaM, niGaRwuH m.

sanskrit.slp1: adarSayan sa taM tasmE prayacCet svaDanAdfRam
sanskrit.word: अदर्शयन् स तं तस्मै प्रयच्छेत् स्वधनादृणम्
sanskrit.iast: adarśayan sa taṃ tasmai prayacchet svadhanādṛṇam

details.body: Liable, a. yogya, aDIna, arha, vaSa in comp.; gen. ex. by arh 1 P, pAtraM, Alu or SIla in comp., or by pot. pass. part.; ‘l(iable) to punishment’ daMqanIya, daMqayogya, daMqArha; ‘l(iable) to be blamed’ niMdApAtraM; ‘l(iable) to fall’ patayAlu, patanaSIla; ‘man is l(iable) to err’ manuzyAH sKalanaSIlAH-pramAdADInAH; See Apt also. 2 anuyogADIna, prazwavya, AhvAnADIna, aBiyojya. [Liable]ness, Liability, s. aDInatA, SIlatA, pAtratA, AlutA in comp.; AhvAnADInatA, anuyogADInatA. 2 (Liabilities) fRaM, udDAraH, paryudaMcanaM.

LIABLE: expr. by circumlo, in default of the principal, a surety who stands to produce him is l. to pay his debt: yo yasya pratiBUstizWeddarSanAyeha mAnavaH. adarSayan sa taM tasmE prayacCet svaDanAdfRam, Kat.: v. Also subject.

LIABLE , a. (Subject to) aDInaH -nA -naM, yogyaH -gyA -gyaM, arhaH -rhA -rhaM, vaSaH -SA -SaM, SIlaH -lA -laM in comp.; ‘liable to be punished,’ daRqayogyaH &c.; ‘liable to death,’ maraRADInaH -nA -naM; ‘liable to disease,’ rogADInaH -nA -naM; ‘not liable,’ anaDInaH -nA -naM. — (Responsible, amenable) AhvAnADInaH -nA -naM, aBi- yoktavyaH -vyA -vyaM, aBiyojyaH -jyA -jyaM, aBiyokturAhvAnADInaH -nA -naM, vyavahAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, vyavaharttavyaH -vyA -vyaM; ‘liable for the debt,’ uttamaRAhvAnADInaH -nA -naM, DanikAhvAnADInaH &c.; ‘he is liable [Page450-b+ 51] to pay,’ dAtum arhati. Sometimes ‘liable’ may be ex- pressed by the affix. Alu; as, ‘liable to fall,’ patayAluH -luH -lu.

LIABLENESS , LIABILITY, s. aDInatA, yogyatA -tvaM, SIlatA; ‘liability to disease,’ rogADInatA; ‘liability to fall,’ patanaSIlatA, patayAlutA. — (Responsibility) AhvAnADInatA, aBiyojyatA, anuyo- gADInatA, vyavahAryyatA; ‘for debt,’ uttamarRAhvAnADInatA, DanikAhvA- nADInatA. — (Debt) fRaM.
Liaison, s. saMbaMDaH, premabaMDaH.
LIAISON: guptapraRayaH: v. Also intercourse.
LIAISON , s. sambanDaH, saMyogaH, premabanDaH, premasambanDaH.
LIAR: (1) miTyAvAdin (f. nI);(2) anftaBAzin (f. RI); etc.: v. False.

LIAR , s. asatyavAdI m. -dinI f. (n), miTyAvAdI -dinI, mfzAvAdI -dinI, asatyavaktA m., ktrI f. (ktf), miTyABAzI -ziRI (n), anftaBAzI &c., anftavAdI &c., anftavAk m. f. (c), anftavadanaSIlaH, asatyavadana- SIlaH, anftI m. (n), ataTyavAdI &c., alIkavAk m., dvijihvaH, anekajihvaH, asatyacUqAmaRiH m.

Libation, s. udaka-dAnaM-taparRaM-pAtanaM-nizekaH, (devatArTaM) peyanizekaH. 2 tarpaRodakaM, nizikta-dravyaM-rasaH, aBiDAraH; ‘to make l(ibation)s to’ udakAdidAnena tfp c., udakaM pat c. or ni-zic 6 P.
LIBATION: aBiGAraH (both of the act and of the liquor), Vi.

LIBATION , s. (The act) udakatarpaRaM, udakadAnaM, udakakriyA, udakanizekaH, udakapAtanaM, devatoddeSakaH peyanizekaH or pAnIyanizekaH or madyanizekaH or peyatyAgaH, pAtrasTarasanizekaH. — (The liquor poured out) tarpa- RodakaM, tarpaRarasaH, tarpaRadravyaM, niziktarasaM, pAtitarasaH; ‘to make li- bations,’ udakAdidAnena or udakAdinizekeRa tfp (c. 10. tarpayati -yituM), devatAmuddiSya pAtrasTarasaM pat (c. 10. pAtayati -yituM) or pAtrasTamadyaM nizic (c. 6. -ziYcati -zektuM) or avasic.

sanskrit.word: न के-वलं यो महतोपभाषते शृणोति तस्मादपि यः
sanskrit.iast: na ke-valaṃ yo mahatopabhāṣate śṛṇoti tasmādapi yaḥ

details.body: Libel, s. pari(rI)vAdaleKaH, apavAda-niMdA-AkzAraRa-leKaH-patraM, piSunaleKa. v. t. pari-vad 1 U, apa-BAz 1 A, aBi-SaMs 1 P, niMdApatreRa kalaMkayati (D.) or Akzar 10; ‘not only he who actually l(ibel)s great persons, but he also who countenances such l(ibel) is guilty’ na ke-valaM yo mahatopaBAzate SfRoti tasmAdapi yaH sa pApaBAk (K. v. 83). [Libel]ler, s. apa-vAdakaH, aBiSaMsakaH, parivAdarataH, aByasU-yakaH, piSunaH. [Libel]lous, a. parivAdagarBa, kalaMkAvaha, apavAdaka, piSuna, kalaMka-duzkIrti-kara (rI f.).
LIBEL (subs.): pari (rI) vAdaleKaH: v. Calumny.
LIBEL (v.): parivAdaM liKati (liK, c. 6.): v. To defame.
LIBEL , s. apavAdapatraM, apavAdaleKaH, apavAdaleKyaM, parivAdaleKyaM, nindApatraM, nindAleKaH, aBiSApapatraM, amukoddeSakaM piSunaleKyaM, kalaNkasUcakapatraM, aKyAtisUcakapatraM.

To LIBEL , v. a. apavAdapatreRa nind (c. 1. nindati -ndituM), nindApatreRa apavad (c. 1. -vadati -dituM) or parivad or kalaNka (nom. kalaNkayati -yituM) or kIrttikalaNkaM kf, amukajanamuddiSya apavAdapatraM liK (c. 6. liKati, leKituM) or nindApatraM liK.
LIBELED , p. p. patrApavAditaH -tA -taM, patraninditaH -tA -taM, patrABiSastaH -stA -staM, leKaninditaH &c., patrakalaNkitaH -tA -taM.
LIBELER , s. patrApavAdI m. (n), patrABiSastakaH, apavAdapatraleKakaH, nindApatraleKakaH, kalaNkakaraH, aByasUyakaH.
LIBELLOUS: parivAdagarBa (f. rBA): v. Calumni- -ous.

[Liberal]ity, s. OdAryaM, vadAnyatA, tyAgaH, dAnaSIlatA, akArpaRyaM, bahupradatvaM, dAtftvaM, atidAnaM. 2 mAhAtmyaM, udAracittatvaM, cittOdAryaM. LIBERAL (adj.): I Catholic: udAraH (rA, raM), for to the l. minded, the (whole) earth is kindred: udAracaritAnAM hi vasuDEva kuwumbakam, H. II. Boun- -tiful:(1) vadAnya (f. nyA), gone to another l. (person): gato vadAnyAntaram, R.;(2) tyAgaSAlin (f. nI), Si.;(3) dAnaSORqa (f. RqA), A.;(4) muktahasta (f. stA) (= open-handed).III Pro- -fuse: q. v.: pracuraH (rA, raM). Ph.: l. arts: uccavidyAH (f. pl.) (?).
LIBERAL (subs.): *udAraH, l. government: *udArARAM SAsanam.

LIBERALITY: I of mind: OdAryam or udAratA. II Munificence:(1) vadAnyatA;(2) tyAgaSAlitA; etc. III. A gift.: dAnam.

LIBERALLY: I Unselfishly: udAram.II Bounti- -fully: muktahastam.III Not strictly: asaMyataH (??); mAvataH (= by purport).
LIBERALLY , adv. bAhulyena, akArpaRyena, atityAgena, atidAnena, muktaha- stena, vadAnyavat, udAravat, bahuSas, ativyayena, sTUlalakzyavat.

LIBERATION: mokzaH, l. of slaves: dAsasya mokzaH, Va.: v. Release.

LIBERATION , s. muktiH f., vimuktiH f., vEmuktaM, mocanaM, vimocanaM, mokzaH -kzaRaM, vimokzaH -kzaRaM, parimokzaRaM, trARaM, paritrARaM, nistAraH, nistaraRaM, udDAraH, udDaraRaM, samudDaraRaM, visarjjanaM, visfzwiH f., muktidAnaM.
LIBERATOR: (1) mokzakaH, pari-;(2) mocakaH, vi-, saM-.
LIBERATOR , s. mocakaH, vimocakaH, mokzakaH, muktidAtA m. (tf), udDarttA m. (rttf), samudDarttA m., nistArakaH, nistArayitA m. (tf), tArakaH, rakzakaH.

Libertine, a. KaMqitavftta, vyasanin, kAma-vizayAsakta, vizayin, Boga-kAma-Asakta, durvftta, nir-a-maryAda, Brazwacaritra, muktamaryAda, durAcAra, vyaBicArin, kAmavftta. s. laMpawaH, kAmukaH, kAmAsaktaH, viwaH, strI-laMpawaH-paraH-se-vin m. [Libertin]ism, s. vyasanaM, vyaBicAraH, lAMpawyaM, vizayAsakti f., Boga-kAma-AsAktiH, durvfttatA, amaryAdA, strIvyasanaM-vyAsaMgaH.
LIBERTINE: (1) KaRqitavftta (f. ttA) (?);(2) magnacAritrayantraRa (f. RA), D. xiii.

LIBERTINE , a. vyasanI -ninI -ni (n), vyasanIyaH -yA -yaM, vyaBicArI -riRI -ri (n), vizayAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, vizayI -yiRI &c., vizayAnu- rAgI -giRI &c., kAmAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, BogAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, kAmukaH kA -kaM, taralaH -lA -laM, anavasTaH -sTA -sTaM, amaryyAdaH -dA -daM, nirmaryyAdaH -dA -daM, durAcAraH -rA -raM, kAmavfttaH -ttA -ttaM.

Liberty, s. svADInatA, svavaSatA, svataMtratA, svAtaMtryaM, anAyattatA, apArataMtryaM, ayaMtraRaM, dAsyABAvaH, adAsyaM, svAcCaMdyaM, svecCAcA-ratA. 2 svecCA, svakAmaH, svaruci f., yadfcCA. 3 anujYA, anumati f. 4 mukti f., mokzaH-kzaRaM, mocanaM. 5 virahaH, aBAvaH, SUnyatA. 6 aDikAraH, kzamatA, Sakti f. 7 karmAvaSatA, dEvAnaDInatA, adEvaparatA. 8 amaryAdA, maryAdAtikramaH, avinayaH, vinayA-tikramaH, vinayollaMGanaM; ‘donʼt take l(iberty) with your teachers’ guruzu avinayaM mA kArzIH; ‘your ladyship is at l(iberty) to do what befits the occasion’ yadatrAvasara-prAptaM tatra praBavati BavatI (Ka. 158); baMDe mokzeca aDunA sA te praBavati (Ka. 354) ‘she is at l(iberty), to detain or set you free’; ‘to set at l(iberty)’ muc 6 P or c. mokz 10; See Liberate; ‘at l(iberty)’ ayaMtrita, niravagraha; See Free.

LIBERTY , s. (Freedom from restraint or servitude) svatantratA, svAtantryaM, svADInatA, anaDInatA, svacCandatA, svAcCandyaM, AtmADInatA, aparADInatA, svavaSatvaM, aparavaSatvaM, avaSatvaM, vivaSatvaM, apAratantryaM, anAyattatA, aparAyattatA, svAyattatA, svecCAcAratA, adAsyaM, adAsatvaM, aparaprezyatvaM, dAsyABAvaH, sevABAvaH, ayantraRaM, niryantraRaM, ayantritatvaM. — (Freedom of the will) svecCA, svacCandatA, svakAmaH, yadfcCA. — (Ability to act) kzamatA, SaktiH f. — (Freedom in general) muktiH f., vimuktiH f., mokzaH, vimokzaH, parimokzaRaM, mocanaM, vimocanaM, vEmuktaM, banDanABAvaH, banDanarAhityaM. — (Leave) anujYA, anumatiH f., aByanujYA. — (Exemption from) muktiH f., virahaH, rAhityaM, SUnyatA, aBAvaH, mokzaH. — (Freedom from necessity) BavitavyAnaDInatA, dEvAna- DInatA, karmmAvaSatA, dEvAvaSatA. — (Breach of decorum) avinayaH, amaryyAdA, vinayAtikramaH, maryyAdAtikramaH, maryyAdAtivarttanaM, maryyAdAticAraH, vinayollaMGanaM; ‘to set at liberty,’ muc (c. 6. muYcati, moktuM), vimuc, mokz (c. 10. mokzayati -yituM), vimokz, nistF (c. 10. -tArayati -yituM); ‘at liberty,’ aniyataH -tA -taM, ayantritaH -tA -taM, niryantritaH -tA -taM, niravagrahaH -hA -haM, kzamaH -mA -maM. See FREE.
LIBIDINOUS: kAmukaH (kI, kaM): v. Lewd, lust- -ful.

LIBRATION , s. tolanaM, samatolIkaraRaM, BAratulyatA, tulyabalatA, tulyatA.
LICE , s. pl. yUkAH m. f. pl., keSakIwAH m. pl., zawpadAH m. pl.

LICENSE (v.): anujAnAti (jYA, c. 9.): v. To permit.

LICENSED , p. p. anujYAtaH -tA -taM, patrAnujYAtaH -tA -taM, gfhItAnujYaH -jYA -jYaM, aByanujYAtaH -tA -taM, anumataH -tA -taM.
LICENSER , s. anujYAdAtA m. (tf), anumatidAtA m., anujYApatraprakASakaH.
LICENTIATE: *labDADikAraH (rA, raM).
LICENTIATE , s. gfhItAnujYaH, sAnujYaH, aDikArayuktaH, aDikArI m. (n).

LICENTIOUSLY , adv. aSizwavat, ucCfNKalaM, vyaBicAreRa, lampawavat, kAmukaM, kAmukavat, vizayAnurAgAt, duzwavat, pApizWavat.

LICHEN , s. SilAvalkA, sUkarI, SUkarI, SUkarAkrAntA, varAhakrAntA.

Bakzayati -yituM), samBakz, gF (c. 6. girati, garituM -rItuM), nigF, saMgF. — (Beat) taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), vetrAGAtaM kf, daRqAGAtaM kf.
LICK , s. lehaH -hanaM. — (A blow) AGAtaH, prahAraH, tAqanaM, daRqAGAtaH.

LICKERISHNESS , s. rasikatvaM, sarasatA, sOrasyaM, mizwatA, svAdutA, lAlityaM.
LICKING (subs.): I lehaH, -nam, etc.II Beating: tAqanam.

Life, s. jIvanaM, jIvitaM, prARavAraRaMprARaDAraRaM, asu-DAraRaM. 2 jIvaH, satvaMsattvaM, jIvitaM, cEtanyaM cetanA, prARavAyuH, prARAtman m., jIvAtmA; ‘endowed with l(ife)’ jIvin, prARin, sajIva, sacetana; ‘love of l(ife)’ jIvitatfzRA, jijIvizA; ‘impatience of l(ife)’ jIvita-dvezaH-trAsaH; ‘deprived of l(ife)’ hataprARa-jIvita, nazwaprARa; ‘support of l(ife)’ prARayAtrA-DAraRaM-rakzaRaM; ‘reckless of l(ife)’ jIvitavyayin, jIvitanirapekza; ‘means of l(ife)’ jIvanopAyaH. 3 (Life-time) Ayus n., jIvitaM, jI-vanaM, jIvitakAlaH, AyurmaryAdA, AyuHpari-mARaM; ‘possessed of long l(ife)’ dIrGAyus, Ayuzmat, cirAyus; ‘for l(ife)’, ‘during l(ife)’ ‘all oneʼs l(ife)’ yAvajjIvaM, AmaraRAt; ‘in all oneʼs l(ife)’ Ajanma, janmataH praBfti or AraBya; ‘my lamp of l(ife) is nearly out’ nirvARaBUyizWo me jIvitapradIpaH or avasita-prAyo me jIvitAvaDiH. 4 (fig.) jIvitaM, prARAH, (tvaM jIvitaM me U. 3). 5 saMsAraH, BavaH, saMsfti f., lokayAtrA, BUlokavAsaH, ihavAsaH. 6 vftti f., AcAraH, vyavahAraH, rIti f., cezwitaM, pravfttiH, vfttaM, AcaraRaM; ‘leading a virtuous l(ife)’ sADuvftta, sadAcAra, puRyamArga. 7 caritaM, caritraM, jIvanavfttAMtaH, caritraracanA-kaTanaM. 8 avasTA, daSA, sTiti f., vfttiH, BAvaH, gati f. 9 utsAhaH, vIryaM, tejas n., satvaMsattvaM, rasaH; ‘bring or restore to l(ife)’ ujjIv c., socCvAsa a. kf 8 U, asUn prAp c., (parIkzitaM durlaBAnasUnprApita-vAn Ka. 175); ‘come to l(ife)’ ujjIv 1 P; ‘active l(ife)’ pravfttiH, pravftti-saMsAra-mArgaH, lokavyavahAraH; ‘retired l(ife)’ nivfttiH, ni-vfttimArgaH; ‘he entered on a military l(ife)’ yoDavfttimASrayata; ‘engaging in public l(ife)’ lokavyavahArapravfttiH; ‘in this l(ife)’ iha, ihaloke; ‘the vicissitudes of l(ife)’ saMsAra-cakraM-parivartanaM, daSAMtarARi; ‘l(ife)-blood’ prARaH, tattvaM, sAraBUtaM dravyaM; ‘l(ife)-giving’ prARada, jIva-da-dAyin; vIryada, utsAhakara (rI f.); ‘l(ife)-guard’ rAjaparicaraH, SarIra-rakzakaH; ‘l(ife)-time’ jIvitAvaDiH, jIvita-kAlaH; ‘during oneʼs l(ife)-time’ yAvajjIvaM. [Life]less, a. gatajIvita, gatAsu, parAMsu, vyasu, gata-nazwa-prARa, hatajIvita, prARa or jIva-rahita or hIna, acezwa. 2 ajIva, nirjIva, vi-a-cetana, cEtanya-hIna-rahita, niScetana. 3 niHsattva, nirutsAha, nistejas, sattva-rasa-hIna.

LIFE: I Of men or animals:(1) jIvanam or jIvitam, I did not quit l.: jIvitaM notsfzwavatI, K.; longing for my own death simply that he may be (recovered) to l.: tajjIvitAyE vAtmamaraRAya spfhayantI, K.;(2) prARAH (m. pl.), takes one's l.: prARAn harati, A r.; my l. is moving (i. e. I am dying): pracalanti hi me prARAH, Vi.; I will give you my l.: [Page417] prARAn te dAsyAmi, A. r.;(3) asavaH, (m. pl.), why my l. did not go out at the time: asavo me tatkzaRe kena hetunA nodgacCanti sma, K. II. Life- -time:(1) jIvanam or jIvitam, the l. of animals consists of four or five days: jIvitaM janmavatAM catuHpaYcAnyahAni, D.; throughout one's l.: yAvajjIvam. H. s.;(2) Ayus (n.), having long l.: dIrGAyus (mfn.), Sr.III Fig.:(1) jIvanam or jIvitam, you are (my) l.: tvaM jIvitam, U. iii. 26.;(2) prARAH, D.IV. Conduct: q. v.: vfttam or vfttiH.V. Vivacity, energy: q. v.: perh. prARAH.

LIGHT (subs.): I Lit.:(1) AlokaH, to give l.: AlokaM dadAti, Si. xx. 38.;(2) prakASaH, like l. and darkness: tamaHprakASavat, S.; by the l. of plants: ozaDiprakASena, Ku. vi. 43.;(3) praBA (= shining l.), l. of the moon: indupraBA Su.;(4) jyotis (n (= 3);(5) tejas (rare), Par.II That which gives 1.:(1) AlokaH, I noticed a l. in the street: rAjavITyAmAlokamalakzayam, D. ii.;(2) pradIpaH (gen. =lamp), l. of knowledge: jYAnapradIpaH, D. III. A window: q. v.: AlokamArgaH, R. vii. 6.VI Fig., publicity: q. v.: prakASatA, to get to l.: prakASatAM gacCati, Mu. To see l. or come to l.: prakASIBavati, Mu. To bring to l.: prakASayati, (nomi.). V. In painting: prakASa- BAgaH (?).VI Illustration: to throw l.: viSadI- karotiH v. To explain.VII Construction: according to one's l.: svavyAKyAnusAreRa. VIII. A noteworthy: tejas (n.) (?). Ph.: l. of coun- tenance i. e. favour: prasAdaH.

Like, a. sadfSa (SI f.), tulya, sama; samAna, sanniBa, anukArin (with gen. or instr.); oft. by upama, niBa, rUpa, viDa, pratima, saMkASa, nIkASa, pratIkASa, BUta, (all in comp.); also by sa or anu in comp.; ‘of l(ike) properties’ saguRa, anuguRa-Darman, sama-tulya-guRa, samaBAva; ‘of l(ike) form’ sarUpa, anurUpa, tulyAkfti, tulyarUpa; ‘l(ike) a father’ pitfBUtaH, pitfsTAnIyaH; ‘of l(ike) class’ sajAti, sajAtIya, savarRa, savarga, tulyavarRa; ‘almost l(ike) Hara’ harakalpa; ‘l(ike) this’ IdfSa-S, etAdfSa-S; ‘l(ike) that’ tAdfS-Sa; ‘l(ike) what’ kIdfS-Sa; ‘l(ike) which’ yAdfS-Sa; ‘l(ike) me, -us’ mAdfSa, asmAdfSa, &c.; ‘l(ike) thee, you’ tvAdfSa, yuzmAdfSa, &c.; ‘l(ike) your honour’ BavAdfSa; ‘to be l(ike)’ anukf 8 U (with gen.), saMvad 1 P (with instr.), anuhf 1 P (with acc.); See Resemble; ‘the son was l(ike) his generating cause (father)’ na kAraRAt svAdviBide kumAraH (R. v. 57); ‘these and the l(ike)’ eva-mAdi; ‘in l(ike) manner’ taTA, evaM, tadvat, taTEva, evameva, evaMviDaM. s. samaH, tulyaH, sadf-SaH, tulyaguRaH, yamakaH-laH; ‘his l(ike) was and will never be seen’ anena sadfSo na BUto na Bavizyati. adv. Ex. by vat in comp., iva, yaTA, nirviSezaM in comp.; ‘l(ike) an earthen pot’ mfdGawavat; often by Karm. or Bah. comp.; ‘black l(ike) a cloud’ meGaSyAma; ‘having a moon-l(ike) face’ caMdra-muKa; ‘brought up l(ike) oneʼs own children’ apatyanirviSezaM saMvarDita; ‘to act l(ike)’ anukf. 2 Likely, q. v. v. t. ruc 1 A (with dat. of person who likes); aBinaMd 1 P, anu-saM-aBi-man 4 A, anumud 1 A, praSaMs 1 P, prI pass., tuz 4 P; ‘does not l(ike) the present’ upAyanaM nABinaMdati, upAyanena na tuzyati &c., snih 4 P, anuraMj pass. (with loc.). v. i. iz 6 P, aBilaz 1, 4 P, ruc; oft. by kAma in comp.; ‘just as you l(ike)’ yaste CaMdaH (V. 3), yadBavate rocate; ‘doing as one l(ike)s’ kAmacAraH, svEravfttaH, svacCaMdaH, svErin; ‘taking what form he l(ike)s’ kAmarUpaH; ‘do what you l(ike)’ yaTABilazitaM kriyatAM. [Like]ness, s. sAdfSyaM, sAmyaM, tulyatvaM, AnurUpyaM, sArUpyaM, tulA, upamA, anukAraH, saMvAdaH, AnuguRyaM, OpamyaM, &c. 2 rUpaM, Akfti f., AkAraH, mUrti f. 3 pratimA-mAnaM, pratirUpaM-kftiH, pratimUrtiH, praticCaMdaH,

LIKE (adj. or adv.): I In gen.:(1) sadfSaH (SI, SaM), it is l. (it) but not the same: sadfSa eza na punaH saH, Mr. ix.;(2) tulyaH (lyA, lyaM) (= matching), you choose him l. you by birth, in beauty, in fresh age: kulena kAntyA vayasA navena tvamAtmanastulyamamuM vfRIzva, R. vi. 79.;(3) with iva in comparing, l. fortune: SrIriva, U.;(4) -vat in comp. (adv.), l. water: jalavat, J.;(5) occasionally by comp., beautiful l. the moon: indusundara (f. rI), Mal. [In such cases, upamaH (mA, maM), -niBaH (BA, BaM), (rarely) -pratimaH (mA, maM), -praKyaH (KyA, KyaM) -pratIkASaH (SA, SaM), etc. may be used in comp.]: v. Also equal, same.II Likely: q. v.

LIKE (v.): (1) expr. with: rocate (ruc, c. 1.) (with dative of the person l.ing), I l. that: tanmahyaM rocate;(2) with prItiH (= pleasure), she did not l. him: na sa tasyAH prItaye baBUva: v. (Be) pleased, love.

LIKE , a. (Resembling) sadfSaH -SI -SaM, sadfkzaH -kzA -kzaM, sadfk m. f. n. (S), tulyaH -lyA -lyaM, samaH -mA -maM, samIyaH -yA -yaM, samAnaH -nA -naM, sanniBaH -BA -BaM, anukArI -riRI -ri (n), nirviSezaH -zA -zaM, prAti- BAsikaH -kI -kaM. The following can only be used in comp. at the end of a word upamaH -mA -maM, niBaH -BA -BaM, pratimaH -mA -maM, upamitaH -tA -taM, praKyaH -KyA -KyaM, saNkASaH -SA -SaM, rUpaH -pA -paM, viDaH -DA -DaM, nIkASaH -SA -SaM, nikAsaH -sA -saM, pratIkASaH &c., pratikASaH &c., pratikAsaH &c., pratIkAsaH &c., BUtaH -tA -taM; ‘like the moon,’ candraniBaH -BA -BaM, candropamaH -mA -maM; ‘like, but with a degree of inferiority,’ kalpaH -lpA -lpaM. The propositions sa and anu are often used indifferently with sama, samAna, and tulya to express ‘like’; as, ‘of like form,’ sarUpaH -pA -pI -paM, anurUpaH -pA -paM, samarUpaH -pA -paM, tulyarUpaH &c., tulyAkftiH -tiH -ti, tulyAkAraH -rA -raM; ‘of like properties or qualities,’ saguRaH -RA -RaM, anuguRaH -RA -RaM, samaguRaH -RA -RaM, tulyaguRaH &c., samAnaguRaH &c., saDarmmA -rmmA -rmma (n), anuDarmmA &c., samAnaDarmmA &c., samaBAvaH -vI -vaM; ‘of like tribe, class, or kind,’ sajAtiH -tiH -ti, sajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, samAnajAtiH &c., samAnajAtIyaH &c., savarRaH -rRA -rRaM, tulyavarRaH &c., saviDaH -DA -DaM, savargaH -rgA -rgaM, savargIRaH -RA -RaM, savargIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘like this or that,’ IdfSaH -SI -SaM, Idfk m. f. n. (S), IdfkzaH -kzA -kzaM, etAdfSaH &c., etAdfk &c., etAdfkzaH &c., tAdfSaH &c., [Page455-a+ 51] tAdfk &c., tAdfkzaH &c.; ‘like what?’ kIdfSaH &c., kIdfk &c., kIdfkzaH &c.; ‘like which,’ yAdfSaH &c., yAdfk &c., yAdfkzaH &c.; ‘like me,’ mAdfSaH &c., mAdfk &c., mAdfkzaH &c.; ‘like thee,’ tvAdfSaH &c., tvAdfk &c., tvAdfkzaH &c.; ‘like your honor,’ BavAdfSaH &c., BavAdfk &c., BavAdfkzaH &c. ‘To be like,’ anukf, sadfSaH -SI -SaM BU, tulyaH -lyA -lyaM BU, sadfSIBU, tulyIBU. The following examples illustrate the use and construction of some of the above words. ‘The son is very like the father,’ putro bahuDA pitur anukaroti or putraH pitfrUpo Bavati; ‘like another son,’ putranirviSezaH -zA -zaM ‘there never has been, nor ever will be, any one like him,’ anena sadfSo na BUto na Bavizyati; ‘there is nobody like him,’ tena sadfSaH kaSci- dapi nAsti or na tasya tulyaH kaScana or na kopi tasya samaH; ‘like the sun,’ AdityasadfSaH -SI -SaM, Adityena tulyaH &c.; ‘a crime like that of Brahmanicide,’ brahmahatyAsamaM pApaM; ‘like me,’ mama samaH or mama tulyaH or mama anurUpaH or madrUpaH &c. o

Since some of the above verbs have a neuter sense, and some of these again are susceptible of an active sense if used in other forms, the construction of the sentence must vary accordingly; thus, ‘I like that,’ tad mahyaM or mama rocate or ahaM tad rocayAmi or tad mayA praSasyate or ahaM tad anumanye or tad mayA anumataM or tad mama aBimataM; ‘he does not like the gift,’ dattaM nABinandati or dattena na tuzyati; ‘they like their king,’ svarAjAnam anuruDyante; ‘he likes his brother's wife,’ BrAtur BAryyAyAm anurajyate; ‘women like everybody,’ sarvve strIRAM priyAH.

The nyAya school was instituted by the sage Gautama, the branch of it called vESezikaM was founded by Kaṇāda. The following are some of the terms of logic; ‘universal pervadence or extension,’ vyAptiH f., aBivyAptiH; ‘extreme extension or conclusion unwarranted by the premises,’ ativyAptiH; ‘individual or particular extension,’ avyAptiH f., avyApyavfttiH f.; sign of the existence of an inherent property, vyAptilakzaRaM; ‘subject of an inference,’ vyApyaM. Other terms are upalaprakzepaH, utTApyAkAMkzA, pravfttinimittaM, kEmarTyaM, vyApyakowiH f., sidDasADanadozaH.

LOSE: I. To cause to be taken: hArayati, apa-, (c. of hf), I. lost ten sovereigns in gambling: daSasuvarRaM dyUte hAritam, Mr.; to l. wife: patnIM hArayati, Vi. v. 23. II To be deprived of: viyujyate (pass. of yuj): v. To deprive, de- -void of.III To fall from: q. v.: BraSyati, -te, pari-, pra-, (BraMS, c. 4.), l.s spirits: praBraSyate tejasaH, Mr.IV Opposed to win: parAjayate (ji, c. l.) (rare), what you first lost: kinnu pUrvaM parAjEzIH, Mah. ii. 67. 7.IV To miss.: expr. with naSyati (naS, c. 4.), pra-, one who has lost his way: pranazwavartman (mfn.), K.; Vasantasenā is lost: nazwA vasantasenA, Mr. i. V. To ruin, destroy: q. v.: nASayati (c. of naS).VI Of time: v. To spend, waste. Ph.: to l. oneself: budDya parityajyate, Mr.

To LOSE , v. a. (Be separated or parted from a thing) hA in pass. (hIyate), prahA, viprahA, parihA, vihA with instr. or some- times with abl. c., BraMS (c. 4. BraSyati, BraMSituM), pariBraMS, viBraMS, praBraMS with abl. c., cyu (c. 1. cyavate, cyotuM), pracyu, vicyu with abl. c., viyuj in pass. (-yujyate) with instr. c., apavft (c. 1. -varttate -rttituM) with abl. of the person; ‘he loses his life,’ prAREH or prAReByo hIyate; ‘he loses his kingdom,’ rAjyAd BraSyati or cyavate, tasmAd rAjyam apavarttate; ‘he loses his friends,’ suhfjjanEr viyujyate. — (Let go, drop) hA (c. 3. jahAti, hAtuM, or caus. hApayati -yituM), vihA, apahA, tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM), parityaj, hf (c. 10. hArayati -yituM), apahf; ‘he lost his life,’ prARAn jahO; ‘he loses his son,’ putraM jahAti; ‘he loses his money,’ DanaM hArayati. — (Ruin, destroy, waste) naS (c. 10. nASayati -yituM), vinaS, praRaS, kzi (c. 5. kziRoti, kzetuM, c. 10. kzayayati, kzapayati -yituM), DvaMs (c. 10. DvaMsayati -yituM), viDvaMs, praDvaMs, vyayIkf, apaci (c. 5. -cinoti -cetuM), kzip (c. 6. kzipati, kzeptuM); ‘he loses his wealth,’ arTaM nASayati; ‘he loses his time,’ kAlaM kzipati, kAlakzepaM or kAlaharaRaM karoti. — (Forfeit) daRq in pass. (daRqyate), BraMS or cyu with abl. c., vaYc in pass. (vaYcyate) with instr. c.; ‘he loses his office,’ svADikArAd BraSyati; ‘he loses his reward,’ PalAd BraSyati or [Page467-a+ 51] Palena vaYcyate. — (Not to win, be defeated) parAjitaH -tA -taM BU, ji in pass. (jIyate), parAji; ‘he loses the battle,’ raRe jIyate. — (Lose the game) akzavatyAM ji or parAji in pass., dyUtakrIqAyAM ji in pass., vidiv (c. 4. -dIvyati -devituM), parAjitaH -tA -taM BU. — (Lose the way) paTAt or mArgAt or paTo BraMS or praBraMS or cyu or vicyu or vical (c. 1. -calati -lituM), paTaBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM BU, vartmava- rjitaH -tA -taM BU. — (Lose one's wits) muh (c. 4. muhyati, mohituM), budDiM hA, budDihInaH -nA -naM BU. — (Lose one's consciousness, lose one's self) cetanAM or cEtanyaM hA, nazwacetanaH -nA -naM BU, murCa (c. 1. mUrCati -rCituM), Bram (c. 4. BrAmyati, BramituM), BrAntabudDiH -dDiH -dDi BU.
To LOSE , v. n. (Be defeated) ji in pass. (jIyate), parAji, parAjitaH -tA -taM BU. — (Decline, fail) kzi in pass. (kzIyate), parikzi, parihA in pass. (-hIyate), DvaMs (c. 1. DvaMsate -situM).
LOSER , s. kzatiprApakaH, hAniprApakaH, apAyaprApakaH, anuBUtakzayaH, prAptA- pAyaH, prAptakzayaH, labDApAyaH, labDahAniH m., apAyaprAptaH, parAjitaH.

LOVE (subs.): I Affection: q. v.:(1) preman (n.), man's l. for woman is inconstant: dayitA- svanavasTitaM nfRAM.. prema, Ku. iv. 28.;(2) praRayaH, are you attached to, or in l. or friendship with her daughter: asti Bavato'syA duhitrA saha prasaktiH praRayaH prItirvA, Mr. ix.;(3) anurAgaH (= fondness), mutual l. is the best thing in matches: itaretarAnurAgo dArakarmaRi parArdDaM maNgalam, Ma. ii.;(4) kAmaH (= amorous l.), for he whom you look would fall in l. with you: yaM hi tvamaBivIkzeTAH sa kAmavaSago Bavet, Mah.; l.-sick: kAmArta (f. rtA), Me.; kAmAturaH (rA, raM), D.; Kalahansaka makes l. to Mandārikā: kalahaMsako mandArikAM kAmayate Ma. i.; l. is cross: kAmo vAmaH, Mr.; l. -stricken: madanaparavaSaH (SA, SaM), manmaTamaTyamAna (f. nA), etc.II = darling: priya (f. yA).III Kindness: dayA, universal benevolence is l.: dayA sarvasuKEzitvam, Mah.IV God of love:(1) kAmaH;(2) madanaH;(3) manmaTaH;(4) kandarpaH;(5) anaNgaH.

Of these lunar days there are fourteen for the waxing, and fourteen for the waning moon; the first lunar day is called pratipad f., pakzatiH -tI f.; the day of new moon is called amAvasI, amAvasyA, amA; ‘the day of full moon,’ pUrRimA, pOrRimA, pOrRamAsI, pUrRenduH m. The eleventh tiTi of each SuklapakzaH or waxing, and kfzRapakzaH or waning moon, is regarded as sacred to Viṣṇu; and the following are the names given by Major Candy for the two ekAdaSI of each month: cEtraH, 1. kAmadA, 2. pApamocanI; vESAKaH, 1. mohinI, 2. varUTinI; jyezWaH, 1. nirjalA, 2. aparA; AzAQaH, 1. SayanI, 2. yoginI; SrAvaRaH, 1. putradA, 2. kAmikA; BAdraH, 1. parivarttinI, 2. ajA; ASvinaH, 1. pASANkuSA, 2. indirA; kArttikaH, 1. boDinI, 2. ramA; mArgaSIrzaH, 1. mokzadA, 2. PaladA; pOzaH, 1. prajAva- rDinI, 2. saPalA; mAGaH, 1. jayadA, 2. zawtilA; PAlgunaH, 1. AmalakI, 2. vijayA. The ekAdaSI of the SuklapakzaH of the months A- zAQaH and kArttikaH are both particularly sacred. On the first, or SayanEkAdaSI, Viṣṇu goes to sleep, and on the second awakes. (Difference of solar and lunar days) kzayatiTiH f.; ‘inauspicious lunar day,’ GAtatiTiH f., dagDati- TiH f.; ‘observance of the fasts and rites of the several lunar days,’ tiTipAlanaM; ‘lunar eclipse,’ candragrahaRaM; ‘lunar measurement,’ cAndramAnaM; ‘the lunar dynasty,’ somavaMSaH. — (Resembling the moon).
